FYI

# There is a part of the data mart generation script that envisions a column-based backfill process:
## Create a separate backfill dbt model with new_metrics only
## Run the backfill dbt model (in prelive, or dev env)
## (This part has not been scripted yet) Generate a SQL statement to update the table in prod, filling in the specific new columns based on the data from the prelive/dev env. Then use the dwh_operations process to execute that SQL (or when the DAP authorisation works then execute the SQL on the dedicated cluster). We decided not to use this process, as it involved manual steps and involving the DAP team to approve the dwh operation etc, while a simple backfill of the whole table only ran for a few hours. Also, we know from experience, that an UPDATE statement can be rather slow, so it’s not obvious that a column level backfill is more efficient than backfilling the whole table (that was true when the table was relatively narrow, not sure it is true any more). Relates back to efficient read-write operations, liquid clustering etcetc. 
# The most optimal solution (at least until recently) was to simply backfill the whole mart for specific data intervals using the dedicated custom_build job in Databricks. We triggered that based on the need, usually after bulk adding new columns. 
# In general, we try to avoid triggering full refresh or other similar things automatically, because we want to be in control of how much compute we use and WHEN we use it (e.g. avoid triggering a full refresh in a situation where we need the regular run to complete on time on Mon morning).

Hi [~accountid:60fbd5e28b1a9b006f13d407] We have reviewed the agreement. The agreement  gives WMCA broad control and pushes all financial, operational, and compliance risks onto the Service Provider.

Please find below all indicated risks. If you want us to add comments directly to the agreement please share editable version with us. 

# Financial & revenue
#* *Fixed concession fee (Clause 1.5, App. B)*
_Risk_: We must pay WMCA a fixed monthly fee regardless of ridership levels.
_Impact_: If demand underperforms, this model could make the scheme financially unviable.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 1.5 so that the concession fee is linked to actual revenues (e.g. a percentage of net revenues, with a floor and cap). This ensures WMCA shares in upside but also that we are protected if demand is lower than expected.
#* *No WMCA payments (Clause 20, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA does not contribute to the cost of core operations.
_Impact_: We absorb all operating and capital costs, even when WMCA changes scope.
_Suggestion_: Insert a new provision under Clause 20 and in Schedule 7 (Change Control) stating that if WMCA requires changes which materially increase our costs (e.g. larger fleet, wider hours of service), WMCA must reimburse or adjust the concession fee to reflect these costs.
#* *Commercialisation restrictions (Clauses 14.7–14.9, 21, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA controls sponsorship, branding, and advertising decisions.
_Impact_: We cannot monetise assets through sponsorship or advertising unless WMCA approves.
_Suggestion_: Redraft Clause 21 to require WMCA not to unreasonably withhold or delay approval of sponsorship opportunities proposed by us. Include a revenue-sharing mechanism (e.g. 50/50) to ensure fairness.
#* *Exclusivity not guaranteed (Clause 4.2, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA may appoint other providers even though the contract states the service is exclusive.
_Impact_: Revenues could be diluted if a competitor enters.
_Suggestion_: Add to Clause 4.2 that if WMCA introduces another provider of similar services, the concession fee must be reduced proportionally, or a renegotiation of terms must take place.

2. Liability & Insurance

* *Broad indemnities (Clauses 40.3–40.5, App. B)*
_Risk_: We indemnify WMCA for claims even if caused by customer misuse.
_Impact_: Unlimited exposure for events outside our control.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clauses 40.3–40.5 so that indemnities only apply where claims are caused by our negligence, fraud, or wilful misconduct.
* *Vandalism and theft (Clause 40.7, App. B)*
_Risk_: We bear the full cost of vandalised or stolen scooters and docking stations.
_Impact_: High exposure in UK cities, where vandalism rates are known to be significant.
_Suggestion_: Modify Clause 40.7 so that WMCA shares responsibility where losses exceed an agreed annual threshold, or so that a vandalism mitigation fund is jointly funded.
* *High insurance requirements (Clause 41, App. B)*
_Risk_: Public liability of £20m and employer’s liability of £10m are above normal UK concession standards.
_Impact_: Substantial premium costs that reduce commercial viability.
_Suggestion_: Reduce Clause 41.1 to require £10m public liability cover, with WMCA funding any additional cover if its policies demand it.
* *Extended liability (Clause 40.10, App. B)*
_Risk_: We remain liable for claims for up to 12 years after contract completion.
_Impact_: Exposure long after revenue streams end.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 40.10 so that liability is capped at 6 years, aligning with the standard UK limitation period for contracts.

3. Operational

* *Strict milestones (Clauses 11–13, 50.3.5, App. B)*
_Risk_: Missing a milestone by more than 10 days is treated as a material breach allowing termination.
_Impact_: Even delays outside our control could trigger termination.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clauses 11–13 and 50.3.5 to provide a 30–60 day cure period for missed milestones, and make termination available only for persistent or material failures.
* *System downtime (Clauses 17, 50.3.9, App. B)*
_Risk_: A system outage of more than 12 hours allows WMCA to terminate.
_Impact_: Harsh sanction for technical problems.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 17 so that termination is only possible if downtime exceeds 48 consecutive hours, and exclude outages caused by third parties or force majeure.
* *Absolute service levels (Clause 5.3, App. B; Schedule 5, App. C)*
_Risk_: Service levels apply regardless of demand fluctuations.
_Impact_: We may be forced to over-resource during spikes in demand.
_Suggestion_: Amend Schedule 5 so that service levels scale proportionally with actual demand (e.g. adjusted KPI thresholds where ridership materially exceeds forecast).
* *Training obligations (Clause 18, App. B)*
_Risk_: We must provide training for WMCA staff and third parties at no cost.
_Impact_: Hidden cost burden.
_Suggestion_: Add to Clause 18 that training for WMCA personnel or third parties will be provided at cost, subject to agreed daily rates.

4. Oversight & Control

* *Audit powers (Clause 36, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can audit us and subcontractors during the contract and for six years after expiry.
_Impact_: Heavy administrative burden and risk of disclosing commercially sensitive information.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 36 to limit audits to once per year, require reasonable notice, and restrict scope to records directly relevant to the contract.
* *WMCA monitors (Clause 35, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can place its monitors permanently in our premises.
_Impact_: Operational disruption and confidentiality concerns.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 35 so WMCA may conduct periodic site visits with 10 working days’ notice, but permanent placement requires our consent.
* *Change control (Clause 33, App. B; Schedule 7, App. C)*
_Risk_: WMCA can change service scope, geography, or hours without compensation.
_Impact_: Costs increase without revenue adjustment.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 33 and Schedule 7 to state that any change materially increasing our costs must trigger a corresponding increase in concession fee or cost recovery.

5. IP, Data & Confidentiality

* *Loss of IP (Clause 37.2.2, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA owns all IP relating to its “Swift” system.
_Impact_: We could lose proprietary developments.
_Suggestion_: Add wording in Clause 37.2.2 clarifying that our proprietary technology, algorithms, and software remain ours, even if integrated into WMCA’s system.
* *FOIA disclosure (Clauses 42, 59, App. B; Schedule 13, App. C)*
_Risk_: WMCA may release our confidential data under FOIA.
_Impact_: Competitors could gain access to sensitive commercial information.
_Suggestion_: Insert a requirement into Clauses 42 and 59 that WMCA must consult us before disclosing and redact commercially sensitive information where possible.
* *Cybersecurity (Clause 39.6, App. B)*
_Risk_: Any data breach or cyber incident is a material breach justifying termination.
_Impact_: Harsh given prevalence of cyber-attacks.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 39.6 so termination only applies to repeated or material security failures not remedied within 30 days

6. Workforce & HR

* *Equality and ethical sourcing (Clauses 26–27, 45, App. B; Schedule 18, App. C)*
_Risk_: Obligations exceed statutory requirements; breach may allow termination.
_Impact_: Extra compliance costs.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clauses 26–27 and Schedule 18 so obligations are limited to compliance with applicable law and “Good Industry Practice.”
* *TUPE exposure (Schedule 27, App. C)*
_Risk_: Staff may transfer to WMCA or the incoming provider at contract end, with costs on us.
_Impact_: Redundancy/transfer cost exposure.
_Suggestion_: Amend Schedule 27 to state that WMCA or the successor operator must bear costs of staff transfer or redundancy at contract end.
* *Parent company guarantee (Clause 65, App. B; Schedule 15, App. C)*
_Risk_: Our parent must guarantee the contract.
_Impact_: Exposes wider group balance sheet.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 65 to allow provision of a performance bond as an alternative, or limit guarantee to the first three years of the concession.

7. Termination & Exit

* *WMCA broad termination rights (Clause 50.3, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can terminate for policy changes, minor breaches, or licence withdrawal; we have very limited rights.
_Impact_: Our investment has no protection.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 50.3 to restrict termination to material, uncured breaches. Add reciprocal rights allowing us to terminate if WMCA materially breaches or fails to perform.
* *Exit obligations (Clauses 51–52, App. B; Schedule 14, App. C)*
_Risk_: We must remove assets at our cost and sell to WMCA at net book value.
_Impact_: Potential loss of asset value.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clauses 51–52 and Schedule 14 to require WMCA to pay fair market value for assets or reimburse removal costs.
* *Ongoing duties (Clause 53, App. B)*
_Risk_: Indemnities, insurance, and confidentiality continue indefinitely post-exit.
_Impact_: Long-term exposure without revenue.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 53 so survival is limited to a maximum of two years after termination/expiry.

8. Other Risks

* *Conflict of interest (Clause 66, App. B)*
_Risk_: Could block us from working with other clients.
_Impact_: Restricts business growth.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 66 so conflicts are limited to “direct and material” conflicts, and provide for disclosure + mitigation instead of prohibition.
* *Change of control (Clause 67, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can terminate if we are acquired.
_Impact_: Restricts investment and M&A opportunities.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 67 so termination only applies if the change of control materially prejudices our ability to perform.
* *Publicity restrictions (Clause 58, App. B)*
_Risk_: Cannot make announcements without WMCA approval.
_Impact_: Limits brand promotion.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 58 to carve out routine marketing/brand communications that do not reference WMCA.

9. Additional Risks

* *Regulatory uncertainty (Clause 50.3.8, App. B)*
_Risk_: Termination if government policy changes.
_Impact_: Our investment could be wiped out by national policy change.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 50.3.8 to include compensation to us for unrecovered investment if termination results from government policy change.
* *Political discretion (Clause 1.7, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can act in “public interest” even if commercially harmful.
_Impact_: May be forced into cost-heavy obligations without protection.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 1.7 so WMCA can only exercise discretion where consistent with the express terms of the contract.
* *Reputational risk (Clauses 14.9, 21.3, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA controls branding.
_Impact_: If poorly managed, our brand could be damaged.
_Suggestion_: Add requirement that branding decisions must not unreasonably prejudice our reputation, with disputes resolved under the dispute resolution procedure.
* *Subcontractor dependency (Clause 30, App. B; Schedule 20, App. C)*
_Risk_: WMCA approval needed for subcontractors.
_Impact_: Slows down supplier onboarding.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 30 so WMCA approval can only be withheld on reasonable, objective grounds (e.g. safety, financial stability).
* *Innovation lock-in (Clause 37.2.2, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA acquires ownership of innovations linked to Swift system.
_Impact_: We may lose valuable IP.
_Suggestion_: Add to Clause 37.2.2 that we retain the right to use such innovations in other markets and projects.
* *Exit competition (Schedule 14, App. C)*
_Risk_: We must hand over data and support a competitor at contract end.
_Impact_: Helps competitors gain advantage.
_Suggestion_: Amend Schedule 14 to limit the scope of information handed over to what is reasonably necessary to ensure service continuity.
* *Force majeure imbalance (Clause 49, App. B)*
_Risk_: WMCA can terminate after 2 months; we only after 6 months.
_Impact_: Unbalanced protections.
_Suggestion_: Amend Clause 49 so both parties have reciprocal rights to terminate after 3 months of continuous force majeure.

# *Legal Basis for Processing Location Data*



Firstly, we want to clarify the difference between the _“Allow all the time_” and _“Allow while using the app”_ location tracking settings:



* _“Allow all the time_” - this means the Bolt Courier Application *(‘App’)* can collect a Courier’s phone’s location as follows:
** The Courier is *offline* (i.e., has explicitly set their status as offline to not provide the delivery services): the Courier’s location is collected only when the App screen is open (active) to assign the Courier to the correct country and city. Bolt does not collect the location of the Courier if the App is closed and the Courier is *offline*.
** The Courier is *online* (i.e., the Courier explicitly chose to set their status as online to provide the delivery services): the location of the Courier is collected when the App screen is open (active) or the App is running in the background.
** In both scenarios, the Courier’s location is not collected when the App is fully closed.
** For clarity, the App is considered to be “running in the background” when a Courier opens another application or returns to their phone’s home screen without closing the original application - the App. In this state, the original application - the App - remains active and can perform tasks even though it is not currently visible on their screen.
* _“While using the app_” - this means the App only collects the Courier’s phone’s location when the App’s screen is open and the Courier is actively interacting with it. Once the Courier puts the App in the background, it stops receiving location updates. This means the App can only access a Courier’s phone’s location when it’s visible on their screen. If the Courier switches to another application or the phone’s screen turns off, the App won’t receive location updates in the background.



To provide delivery services via the Bolt Food Platform, Couriers are required to grant Bolt the permission to access their location data in "_Allow all the time_" mode. It is important to note that Bolt does not continuously collect the Courier’s phone location data when "_Allow all the time_" permission is granted. It allows access to the Courier’s location data both when the App screen is open and running in the background, enabling critical features such as facilitating deliveries, calculating estimated delivery time, and tracking the progress of deliveries. h3. _Response to request for clarification_

# *_Bolt’s role and General Terms for consumers._*


_Bolt Operations OÜ operates the Bolt Food platform, and the conditions for handling platform user complaints are set out in Chapter 5 of the General Terms:_ [https://bolt.eu/et-ee/legal/tnc-delivery-client/?category=delivery|https://bolt.eu/et-ee/legal/tnc-delivery-client/?category=delivery|smart-link] _; (the “General Terms”)._

*_1.1._* _Bolt Operations OÜ, which operates the Bolt Food platform, is not the seller of the goods offered on the platform nor the provider of the delivery service. Therefore, Bolt has no statutory obligation to resolve consumer complaints or issue refunds regarding the quality of purchased goods or the delivery service, which are provided by independent third-party merchants and couriers._

*_1.2._* _Nevertheless, in order to ensure a positive user experience, Bolt provides support to find the quickest and fairest solution for all parties in cases where problems arise with the quality of goods or their delivery. In certain cases, if Bolt has reasonable grounds to believe that the consumer complaint is justified, Bolt may offer a refund for the respective order. To assess the matter, Bolt may request additional information or evidence from the consumer, such as photos or other details, which are compared with information received from the merchant or courier._

*_1.3._* _If the consumer is not satisfied with the solution offered by Bolt or wishes to resolve the matter directly with the merchant or courier, the consumer may and is even encouraged to contact them directly. The merchant’s contact details (such as email address and phone number) are always available under the merchant’s profile on the Bolt Food platform, regardless of whether the consumer is logged into their account. During an active order, the consumer can contact the courier directly through the app using the special contact function visible on the active order screen._

*_1.4._* _If the consumer wishes to contact the courier after the order has already been delivered, cancelled, or otherwise completed, they can find the courier’s full name on the e-invoice sent via email. If additional contact details are required, the consumer may request them from Bolt’s customer support. The above is also reflected in Chapter 5 of the General Terms._

*_1.5._* _Clear and simple instructions on how to act or how to contact the merchant, courier, or Bolt’s customer support regarding common questions or other issues are also easily accessible in the Bolt Food app, in the Support section under Help Articles._

----

# *_Internal complaint handling._*


_Bolt operates one of the largest support networks in Europe and globally, employing over 3,000 customer support (CS) specialists, approximately 460 of whom are direct employees. Together, they handle approximately 3 million customer inquiries each month. Support is provided through multiple channels: in-app support (chat), phone, email, and social media. The internal support team is spread across 21 countries, enabling 24/7 multilingual coverage. Twenty global service providers handle over 95% of first-level inquiries under strict service-level and quality agreements, while Bolt retains oversight, escalation, and management responsibilities. All complaints are handled according to the principles of legality, transparency, timeliness, and compliance with consumer protection requirements. The processes are designed to protect consumer rights, ensure service quality, and collect continuous feedback to improve services._

*_2.1. Organisational responsibilities:_*

* *_First-level support:_* _Complaints are received and registered by first responders (in-app support, phone, chat, email, or social media)._
* *_Escalation:_* _Complex or sensitive cases (e.g., safety, fraud, regulatory matters) are forwarded to special teams or higher-level managers._
* *_Oversight:_* _Customer experience and compliance units provide management and oversight, ensuring complaint handling is in line with internal policies and legal norms._
* *_Responsibility:_* _Final responsibility for the quality and timeliness of complaint resolution lies with management._

*_2.2. Complaint handling stages:_*

* *_Receipt and registration_* _– Complaint is registered in the customer management system (e.g., Beehive/Admin). Consumer receives acknowledgment of receipt._
* *_Initial review (triage)_* _– Complaint is categorised and assessed by first-level support; simpler cases are resolved immediately, more complex ones escalated._
* *_Investigation_* _– Escalated cases are reviewed by the relevant team, involving related parties if necessary (e.g., restaurant, courier)._
* *_Resolution proposal_* _– Drafted based on facts, internal policies, and consumer rights obligations._
* *_Communication with the consumer_* _– Outcome is communicated clearly, with reasoning and possible remedies or compensation._
* *_Closure and feedback loop_* _– Case is closed in the system, and insights are channelled into training, knowledge management, and process improvements._

*_2.3. Structured guidelines for customer support:_*

*_2.3.1._* _Bolt has created clear guidelines for agents to ensure consistency, transparency, and compliance in handling complaints. Problems are classified from the consumer’s perspective, not by technical root cause. Agents follow the internal “Issue Adding Guideline,” which contains definitions, examples, and escalation rules._

*_2.3.2._* _Complaints are divided into categories with predefined problem types, descriptions, and reference materials. These are tailored to business areas (ride-hailing, rentals, delivery, etc.) and, where necessary, to the specifics of the local market._

*_2.4. Example:_* _Under seven global consumer complaint categories, there are 87 standard complaint reasons:_

* _Account (13 standard reasons)_
* _App (13 standard reasons)_
* _Support and product quality (1 standard reason)_
* _Services (28 standard reasons)_
* _Order adjustment (11 standard reasons)_
* _Payments (20 standard reasons)_
* _Uncategorized (1 standard reason)_

----

# *_Compensation mechanisms._*


_Refunds to customers are determined by the compensation guidelines, a translation of which is attached to this response._

*_3.1._* _Bolt Operations OÜ provides a platform service, and the provision of customer support is part of the service that service providers (merchants, couriers) “purchase” from Bolt. Consumers always have the right to direct their complaint to the service provider (i.e., the merchant, courier) if the solution offered by Bolt is not acceptable to the consumer._

*_3.2._* _If Bolt issues a refund based on a consumer complaint, it is then settled with the service provider._

*_3.3._* _In exceptional cases, where it is necessary to ensure the safety of customers, Bolt Operations OÜ may decide to remove the service provider from the platform._

----

# *_Communication channels._*


_Communication channels differ by market, and in Estonia two channels are open to consumers – in-app chat and email (_[_estonia-food@bolt.eu_|mailto:estonia-food@bolt.eu]_)._

----

# *_Language of communication._*


_Customer support is offered in local languages – in Estonia, both Estonian, Russian, and English are available. The language of customer support depends on the user’s interface language set in the app (which can be changed under app settings)._

*_5.1._* _If the user has set Estonian as the interface language, they are connected with an agent who speaks Estonian._

*_5.2._* _In every market, proper communication in the local language is ensured, and before an agent can start work, they must meet at least the minimum requirements set for customer support agents._

*_5.3._* _Bolt’s customer support services are mostly provided by Bolt’s service provider partners, but for security-related matters, consumers are offered the possibility to receive customer support in Estonian (24/7) from Bolt’s internal customer support team._

*_5.3.1._* _Primary option: If local language (e.g., Estonian) agents are available, complaints are handled fully in the local language._

*_5.3.2._* _Queue or delay: If there is temporarily a waiting queue for responses or Estonian-language support is limited, the consumer is presented with a choice: (1) wait until an Estonian-speaking agent becomes available; or (2) continue in English, which ensures faster handling of the complaint._

----

# *_Use of artificial intelligence and automated responses._*


_Bolt uses an LLM (Large Language Model) agent in customer support, and the initial triage is performed with the help of the LLM agent. Based on the phrases used by the customer, the customer is directed to the correct customer support team and assigned the correct priority level._

*_6.1._* _The use of artificial intelligence on Bolt platforms ensures the ability to respond quickly and accurately to customer inquiries, providing them with the necessary information and resolving cases around the clock._

*_6.2._* _A customer inquiry directed to artificial intelligence may be automatically forwarded to a customer support specialist for further handling if the artificial intelligence is unable to resolve the inquiry after several exchanges of comments/responses._

*_6.3._* _Certain inquiries deemed more important/risky, such as those related to security and personal data, are usually forwarded immediately by artificial intelligence to a customer support specialist for resolution._

----

# *_Retention of communication._*


_Communication between the consumer and the courier, merchant, and customer support that has taken place through the Bolt Food app remains accessible to all parties for 60 days from the last conversation. In Bolt’s internal databases, the same communication is accessible for three years from the last conversation._

*_7.1._* _Privacy notice for customers –_ [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-eaters/?category=delivery|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/privacy-for-eaters/?category=delivery|smart-link]  _– Section 8._

# *_Analysis of inquiries._*


_Each time a Bolt Food platform user contacts customer support through the app, they can at the end rate their experience on a scale of 1–5 and leave feedback. Insights Managers analyse lower ratings to identify deficiencies and opportunities for process improvements. Program Managers receive the analysis results and, in cooperation with customer support process designers, make improvements to internal customer support guidelines or pass instructions to the customer support operations department to improve quality and conduct additional training._

*_8.1._* _Bolt maintains a DSAT (Customer Dissatisfaction) register, in which all customer interactions that did not receive a high rating are recorded. By way of background: on the Estonian market, approximately 0.005% of all orders placed through the platform end up in the DSAT register. During the period 24.06.2026 – 15.09.2025 (84 days), 98 DSAT entries were recorded by customer support specialists in the Estonian market:_

*_8.2._* _Of these 98 cases, in 19 instances customer support issued a refund to the consumer, in 2 cases the consumers refused compensation, and in 77 cases no refund was made._

*_8.3._* _Root causes of consumer dissatisfaction (reasons for inquiry):_

* _In 10 cases, the wrong products were delivered._
* _In 3 cases, the consumer wanted to cancel the order._
* _In 6 cases, the products did not meet expectations._
* _In 8 cases, the food arrived cold._
* _In 11 cases, items were missing from the order._
* _In 8 cases, the order did not arrive at all._
* _In 14 cases, the order was delayed._
* _In 4 cases, no courier was found._
* _In 34 cases, the issue was categorised as “other.”_

*_8.4._* _Analysis of the root causes of the DSAT entries showed that:_

* _In 6 cases, the preparation of the customer support specialists could have been better._
* _In 11 cases, the issue was related to the courier._
* _In 29 cases, the consumer disagreed with the compensation._
* _In 9 cases, the consumer felt that the customer support specialist did not understand their concern._
* _In 9 cases, the reason was “guideline too rigid.”_
* _In 6 cases, the reason was “compensation guideline too rigid.”_
* _In 4 cases, the reason was “other.”_
* _In 2 cases, the customer support specialist’s communication was too bureaucratic._
* _In 21 cases, the root cause remained undetermined._
* _In 1 case, the reason was process complexity._

*_8.5._* _The same data are collected for all markets where Bolt Food operates. After collecting and analysing DSAT feedback, compensation guidelines are updated: each customer inquiry is grouped according to the reason for contact, explaining why customer support was contacted. Insights Managers analyse the groups of reasons with the highest number of inquiries to identify gaps in existing guidelines and improve processes. Program Managers receive the analysis and, in cooperation with customer support process designers, organise additional training for customer support specialists and ensure updates to existing processes._

# *_Handling consumer complaints._*


_If consumers submit a complaint to TTJA or ECC, the process is as follows:_

*_9.1._* _In cases related to consumer protection authorities, customer support (CS) only performs the initial review of the inquiry, collects necessary information if possible, and forwards the case for further resolution and preparation of a response to the responsible legal counsel for the respective market. These cases are handled on a case-by-case basis, and therefore the customer support analytics team is currently unable to collect sufficient data for process improvement analysis. If shortcomings or areas for improvement in the customer support process are identified during a specific case, the responsible legal counsel may involve the responsible contacts from the customer support experience (CS Experience) unit, who may request the Program Manager to review the existing guidelines._

*_9.2._* _If a complaint is received at the address_ [_registry.notices@bolt.eu_|mailto:registry.notices@bolt.eu]_, the owner of that mailbox forwards the letter to the responsible department (e.g., Bolt Food Local Operations – hereinafter LOPS). All incoming customer complaints are registered in a separate internal register._

*_9.3._* _LOPS collects the facts and evidence related to the complaint (e.g., customer communication, times, order acceptance, etc.). In the collection of evidence and formation of a position, the legal counsel responsible for the specific market is generally responsible._

*_9.4._* _The local legal counsel assesses whether Bolt’s conduct may have been in conflict with the applicable General Terms (referred to in point 1) or whether the restaurant or courier may have failed to fulfil their obligations. If the facts are sufficiently clear, then LOPS prepares the response to TTJA and attaches the evidence._

*_9.5._* _If the compensation amount claimed is small, then in the interest of a positive user experience, Bolt may refund the claimed amount even if it was submitted against the wrong merchant or courier, or if all the facts cannot be fully established._

*_9.6._* _If the compensation amount claimed is large (e.g., Bolt Drive damage claims), then a full response is prepared for the claimant, taking into account reliable evidence from all parties before making a final decision on compensation._

*_9.7._* _If the disputed amount is large, the facts of the dispute are clear, but the decision is in favour of the consumer, then generally Bolt continues the dispute in district court. This occurs mainly in the context of the Bolt Drive service, where disputed amounts can reach several thousand euros._

*_10. Ensuring customer support quality._*
_As described earlier (see response no. 8), Bolt’s focus is on the continuous improvement of processes. At the global level, Bolt uses approximately 2,500 customer support processes and guidelines, covering both specific and more general situations. Changes in customer support processes may arise from consumer, merchant, and courier complaints or feedback, as well as from platform development or internal process optimisation. Since root causes are continuously analysed and improvements are made on an ongoing basis – whether large or small – it is difficult to point to one specific reason that would have prompted changes in customer support processes and guidelines globally or in Estonia during the last 12 months._

----

*_11. The Cyprus KFC offer._*

*_11.1._* _KFC sells bucket meals and similar products (“bucket meals”) usually at a bundled price, which is lower than the combined price of the individual items contained in the bucket meal. This so-called internal discount applied by KFC (approximately 40%) is not displayed in the Bolt Food app as a separate campaign, but is simply shown as the standard sales price of the bucket meal. For example, the “Champions Feast Bucket” was available in the app for €25.95, although if the products included in the bucket meal were purchased separately, their total value would have been higher (e.g., €46.10)._

*_11.2._* _In the case of the campaign in question, KFC informed us that the bucket meal was already sold with an internal discount equivalent to 40%. Therefore, KFC displayed the final price of €25.95 for the bucket meal in the Bolt Food app._

*_11.3._* _As part of the campaign, Bolt wanted to create an exclusive offer by reducing the price even further below KFC’s internal discount. For this purpose, Bolt subsidised an additional 10%, turning KFC’s approximately 40% internal discount into a visible 50% discount for consumers. Therefore, the bucket meal was displayed with a price of €23.05 along with the “-50%” label, calculated from the reference price of €46.10 (which corresponded to the total price of the individual products making up the bucket meal)._

*_11.4._* _The application of Bolt’s additional 10% subsidy created operational issues in the app, since KFC Cyprus operates through two different franchisees with different pricing methods. This caused inconsistencies in discount display mechanisms. Specifically: (1) in some cases, consumers only saw the final price (€25.95 or €23.05) without the previous reference price; (2) in other cases, both the reference price (e.g., €46.10 or €41.10 depending on the product, i.e., the total sum) and the discounted price were shown. Thus, on different dates, different reference prices were displayed (€46.10, €41.10, or none at all). These discrepancies caused confusion about the actual “previous price” of the product. In short – the problem arose from the combination of KFC’s pricing model (bucket meal bundled price without promotional marking) and Bolt’s additional joint campaign, compounded by technical differences in KFC franchise integrations._

*_11.5._* _Upon discovering these technical inconsistencies, we immediately took the following actions: (1) restored the original discounted price of the KFC bucket meal to €25.95, (2) postponed the project under which Bolt’s additional discounts would be added to bucket meals, (3) undertook to ensure technical consistency across all KFC franchisees before launching such discount campaigns, and (4) implemented requirements for correct discount display for all integrations related to KFC._

*_12. Concerning the consumer complaints listed in the TTJA request._*

*_12.1. Bolt Food and food delivery:_* _The consumer can set the delivery address in the app and must confirm the address before the order is confirmed. The consumer has a duty of care to check that the entered delivery address is correct and, if necessary, to notify customer support as early as possible of the need to change the address. If the consumer makes an error and the address needs to be changed, customer support will attempt to change it as quickly as possible, provided the consumer has contacted support and it is still feasible for the courier to adjust the route. For example, if it becomes apparent that the consumer has not informed support of the need to change the address within 20 minutes of placing the order, changing the address becomes difficult._

*_12.2._* _If the consumer fails to notify of the address change, does so too late, does not appear at the agreed location at the time indicated in the app, does not answer calls from the courier waiting at the agreed location, or if the route change is unreasonably long, making it impossible for the courier to deliver the order (e.g., due to traffic and thereby unreasonably delaying the delivery of subsequent orders – see General Terms clause 4.2), Bolt has the right to cancel the order on behalf of the courier and charge the consumer the full order price (see General Terms clause 7.2)._

*_12.3._* _In the context of consumer complaints, we have also investigated courier actions (or inactions) and, where it has been evident that the courier did not deliver the order to the agreed address or did not wait there long enough, Bolt has refunded the full order amount to the consumer._

*_12.4. Bolt Food and food quality:_* _Bolt Operations OÜ is a platform and does not sell food or control the work organisation of merchants operating on the platform. If the consumer submits a justified complaint about food quality (e.g., something missing, food cold, etc.), Bolt may, in justified cases, issue a refund in accordance with the compensation guidelines. If the consumer complaint indicates that the merchant has recurring quality problems, then under Bolt’s agreement with the merchant, Bolt has the right to temporarily suspend or permanently terminate the merchant’s use of the platform. Consumers always have the right to address their complaint directly to the merchant (see response 1.3 above)._

*_12.5. Bolt Drive:_* _This service is provided by Bolt Services EE OÜ, while Bolt Operations OÜ provides the platform service. Bolt Drive can only be used in designated service areas, and rides can also only be ended at designated locations. These restrictions stem from local regulations or the need to ensure the safety of the Bolt Drive user or other road users. If the ride is not ended in the designated area, the consumer is charged for the time during which the vehicle remained idle, as the vehicle was still under the consumer’s control. Similar situations have been analysed in consumer complaints in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. In some cases, Bolt may grant discounts, for example, if the consumer forgot to end the ride. However, there are clear limits to discounts – even when the vehicle was standing idle, Bolt continued to incur fixed costs (leasing, leasing interest, insurance). In other words – we can accommodate the consumer to some extent, but we cannot provide the service below the cost that Bolt pays for the use of the vehicle._

*_12.6. Ride-hailing services:_* _Bolt Operations OÜ does not provide transport services, but operates a platform service for service providers (vehicle owners/fleets/service providers) and customers (consumers/business customers). Ride-hailing service providers are not under our control, and we cannot influence drivers’ activities. They are free to provide services at their own discretion, provided that the accepted order is fulfilled and the order fulfilment is safe for the customer. In certain cases, we have received complaints where the ride starting point set by the customer and the point transmitted to the driver were different. Without delving into technical details – this is something that can be considered the responsibility of the platform, and in such cases the order is compensated by Bolt, since the discrepancies arose from technical errors of the platform._

Some points about the payload from my side:

# Source and Granularity - We don’t actually fully know where user came from nor does webview know the depth, we just invoke the api when we should redirect to chat and in response get some data to show. We have access to user path, for an example on first step with order selected - {{['completed_ride', 'completed_ride.rider']}} vs first step without an order - {{["orderless_case"]}} Right now, if there is no context (order/issue) selected, we show the orderless view. So in theory we can hard code the values you have provided - recent_order/contact_agent. But ideally I want to move all the business logic to a single place - backend. So in long term, I’m thinking if it would make more sense to send the user path array to mixpanel?
# Vertical and user persona - do we need both? Right now, webview only has knowledge of persona and we don’t have mapping of personas to vertical currently. And ideally, I would like to not add this dependency (it would mean, everytime we add a new persona, we also need to add a vertical to it). We can however send persona + app_type combination.
# Category - this is related to nr 1 above. When opening issue selection, we don’t exactly know (on webview side) what step the user is on. We call our api where we pass selected order, case id and current user path. In return we get context, which consists of order context and issue context. This is used to render the data shown in top. Order context has info about date, price, icon url and destination. Issue context has icon_url, category and subcategory (both translated to users language).

Some points about the events:

# Exit/BackButton_Clicked - this button is controlled by native app. Meaning we (webview) don’t know anything about it. Essentially same as if someone force closed the app. While if someone clicked back, webview in theory is still alive, from our POV we don’t know if user clicked back or clicked on an issue and went forward. In both situations, we just take the user path from url and try to fetch list of items to show for current screen.

Expired cards can be used for payments. This looks ok. 
This is happening due to a feature called account updater. Every card has a token, when a card expires the token will remain the same. If the customer pays with an “expired” card then Bolt is able to charge the correct bank account through the card token. 

ChatGPT said: 

The *Account Updater* service keeps stored card details (like card numbers or expiration dates) current when a customer’s card is reissued, expired, or replaced. Merchants or payment processors enrolled in the program automatically receive updated details from the card networks, which helps recurring or saved payments continue without interruption. This reduces declines, protects revenue, and improves the customer experience.

Similar to point one - if merchant went online, then opportunity is closed won. Field requirements are for AMs to fill in order to close opportunities.



Also noting for the call to discuss closing losing the opportunities by AM:

* Current setup: AM only adds inputs, and the next day Salesforce closes wins the opportunity for merchants confirmed churn.
* To-be setup: AM adds inputs and closes loses the opportunity. If the churn reasons and all the relevant fields are inputed, but opportunity is not manually closed lost by AM, then Salesforce can close lose it the next day.

Why we need closing-losing the opportunity? Because it is intuitive - opportunity is an opportunity to bring back the account. If we couldn’t prevent the churn, then we lost the opportunity (doesn’t necessarily mean that it is bad thing, just that account is offline, there is an opportunity to bring them back. We lose them when we can’t, and we won them when we can.

My conclusions:

# The turn on delay helps to avoid the oscillations during turn on - this ensures that the IoT will boot in normal cases, such as battery swap.
# For EB1, If battery is removed and the discharge circuit is active, then the 24V bus is discharged to 1.3V in about 1.5s. 
## If the discharge circuit is not active, then the 24V bus is discharged to 6.6V in about 1.5s and the voltage drops slowly afterwards, in about another 1.5s, the 1.3V is reached. That is the most critical area to avoid - the IoT regulator starts it’s booting sequence when the 24V bus (Vbus) voltage is about 3.25V. Therefore it is important to discharge the bus quickly below 3V to shut off the device to avoid the UVLO from happening.
### For this reason, I think the discharge circuit is important.
# The current shut-down oscillation is in my opinion acceptable - the Voltage oscillation amplitude is above the critical 3-4V window compared to previous regulator. The oscillation stops at about 9V.
# If the 24V regulator is started up, the EB1 IoT introduces 6.5V drop on the 24V bus for about 1 ms. This should be OK as 17V is well above the critical UVLO threshold voltages.
# If there is a specific voltage drop or power cut for specific time, it is possible to trigger the UVLO protection for the IoT regulator - See post from September 26 in the thread below.

When a rider purchases a ticket through the Nilipe app, they will receive a confirmation message with a link  (to add value to their purchase by giving them early access to a discount code). This link will direct them to the Bolt app, where they can claim and book a discounted ride

The discount will be *geo-locked to the specific event location* and valid within a defined timeframe (e.g., up to 4 hours before the event). Each event will have a *dynamic promo code*, allowing riders to use it for *two rides only* (pick-up and drop-off to/from the venue).

As the ride booking and processing take place entirely within the Bolt app, there is *no intergration nor using ride book* beyond the link/promo distribution.

After reviewing the provided information, I do not see major risks, but I would like to highlight a few circumstances that require attention:

# *P2B requirements (Comms align with Art. 3, 4 and 5 obligations)*

* Clearly explain to all drivers / fleets:
** why Priority is displayed above Standard (ranking reason),
** what the pricing logic is (higher than Standard, higher earnings for drivers),
** that they are auto-enrolled and how they can opt out (visible opt-out toggle in-app).
* Information must be available in Finnish and Swedish.

# *Reclass risk (Must avoid reclassification and maintain transparency under Arts. 4, 5, 7–11)*

* To avoid the impression of “employer control”:
** stress that drivers decide themselves whether to participate and whether to accept a ride,
** send the same information to fleets at the same time as to drivers.

# *Consumer Protection / pricing transparency*

* Riders must see clearly that this is a *separate category*, not an extra “fast-track fee.”
* Before booking, riders must be informed that Priority may be more expensive because of shorter ETA and higher acceptance likelihood.

# *Practical points*

* Check that *price bidding* is not being tested in Finland in parallel with Priority (would confuse users and undermine adoption).
* Ensure invoices and tax reporting are handled identically to Standard (Priority only differs on price/earnings).
* Translation: all notifications and terms must be available in Finnish + Swedish.

* We need to ensure that this is not framed or perceived by riders as paying a booking fee or anything similar in order to get matched faster - the faster matching is happening because the drivers earns more.

Hi [~accountid:712020:f8c30920-765a-42dd-bbe7-058336c97a0c] 

We have reviewed the NDA and while we are mindful that you would like this finalised asap the NDA does not meet Bolt contracting standards and leaves Bolt exposed to risk. 

Given the low-risk nature of the engagement and our desire to maintain a good commercial relationship, most terms are acceptable. However, there are a few high-risk clauses that we recommend revisiting or flagging before signature:

# *Clause 5 – Third-Party Liability*
The NDA holds Bolt fully liable for any breaches by employees or external contractors. We propose clarifying that Bolt will take reasonable steps to ensure compliance, rather than assuming indefinite liability.
# *Clause 6 – Mandatory Disclosure*
The disclosure process in legal situations is overly burdensome (e.g., requiring legal opinions and third-party confirmations). We recommend simplifying this to standard legal notice and limitation language.
# *Clause 11 – Indemnity*
The NDA includes a broad indemnity obligation. This is not typical for mutual NDAs and may create unintended liability. We propose limiting this to actual damages for breaches.
# *Clause 12 – Unilateral Amendments*
Huawei currently reserves the right to unilaterally update the NDA via its website. This creates unacceptable legal uncertainty. All changes should be mutually agreed.
# *Clause 14 – Governing Law and Jurisdiction*
The agreement is governed by Chinese law with jurisdiction in Shenzhen. This may not be enforceable or practical for Bolt. A neutral jurisdiction should be proposed if Huawei is open to negotiation - we recommend London, England. 

*Note:* If the customer accepts Bolt Business Terms & Conditions, those will govern confidentiality going forward and override conflicting provisions in the Huawei NDA — but any pre-T&Cs disclosures may still be governed by this NDA.

Based on some basic investigation caching might be very reasonable. The endpoint receives 1.14K requests/sec and we have ~100 balance update events per sec. This means that only ~9% of the cases it is valid to actually request the data again, 91% of the cases nothing has changed. One potential drawback is event lag/latency issues. It’s worth adding a metric to have an understanding. In case it’s more than ~9-10sec we would start to show incorrect prices.

Alternatively check if we can introduce an endpoint in driver-earnings service, since it already does caching, but question if at the end of the day, or even on the go. This would be a similar solution but caching & calculation in a different place.

Improving the query is possible but we wouldn’t benefit much. Introducing a new endpoint that efficiently calculates this information without cache might be just added complexity, and we’d work from different sources, that down the line can lead to discrepancies.

From my read of the Taxi Act (§7) and the linked guidance, it does look like the Danish authorities check for criminal convictions before issuing a driver’s card. The key wording is that the applicant must _not have been convicted of a criminal offense that gives rise to a “nærliggende fare for misbrug”_ (an imminent risk of misuse of the driver’s card), cf. Penal Code §78(2).

So, in practice:

* Not *every* conviction is disqualifying, but those that suggest a risk of misuse (e.g. violence, sexual offenses, financial crimes, etc.) are.
* The Ministry of Transport / relevant authority makes that assessment before granting the card.
* This implies that drivers holding a valid card have already passed that background scrutiny, which should give us some reliance in operations but not for all B2G tenders or B2B contracts 

Thus, it is not a blanket ban on _all_ convictions — only those deemed relevant under §78(2). If we need 100% certainty (e.g. for contractual representations or privacy law reliance), it could still be worth asking external counsel to confirm how the screening is applied in practice and whether supplementary checks are expected of operators.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Summary:* If left as-is, these clauses create risks for Bolt around *information security assurance, GDPR compliance, and oversight of sub-processors*. Further negotiation is recommended. 

Details:

* *Security measures (Clause 3.2.3)* – City Legal refuses to reference Bolt’s Infosec standard. We requested City Legal’s own security measures for review.
** *Risk:* supplier’s measures may be weaker than Bolt’s standard requirements, increasing exposure to data breaches.
** *Action point*: Once provided, we advise to forward them to Infosec for review and approval - this is a necessary step if a supplier does not agree to reference our Infosec standard.
* *Data breach notification (Clause 3.2.6)* – based on current drafting, Bolt will only receive a short notification regarding an occurred data breach and then Bolt can request further details from the supplier if necessary. By standard, Bolt requires more comprehensive initial notification re/ the breach, which is required to meet our GDPR reporting obligations.
** *Risk:* Bolt could be unable to assess the breach as reportable and notify regulators on time, leading to compliance failures and potential fines.
* *Sub-processor notification (Clause 3.3(e))* – Wording may not give Bolt sufficient visibility or control over new sub-processors.
** *Risk:* While the practical risk is low, the clause limits Bolt’s ability to object effectively to sub-processors. Without receiving adequate details in the initial notification, Bolt may be unable to properly assess compliance risks before the sub-processor is engaged. This could result in reputational or regulatory exposure if unsuitable sub-processors are engaged by City Legal.

* *Exclusion of indirect/consequential losses*: The clause excludes loss of data, reputational harm, loss of contracts, revenue, and goodwill—exactly the types of damage likely to result from a personal data breach.

Hi Neeraj,

Feel free to share the following to Expedia:

_We suggest a few targeted adjustments to align with our standard approach._

* _Residuals Clause: Removed to ensure confidential information, even if remembered, cannot be reused without express permission._
* _Governing Law: Proposed shifting to England and Wales as a neutral yet commercially familiar jurisdiction._

_We believe these changes keep the spirit of your draft intact while ensuring clear protections for both sides._



If Expedia pushes back and insists on signing the NDA as-is, we can proceed, but with eyes open to the following implications:

* Residuals Clause: There's a risk that ideas, techniques, or strategies disclosed could be used indirectly by Expedia under the residuals carve-out — especially difficult to monitor or enforce.
* Governing Law – Washington State: Dispute resolution would occur in the U.S., which increases legal cost, logistical complexity, and may tilt enforcement outcomes toward Expedia’s home jurisdiction. Proceeding would require confidence that material disputes are unlikely.

In either case, the business benefit of engaging with Expedia may outweigh these risks — just flagging them so teams are aware.

Cheers,[^Non-Disclosure Agreement (Bolt Operations OÜ and Expedia, Inc.).docx]

I've reviewed the case and everything is correct on Bolt's end. The preauthorisation was successfully released, and there is no further action required from us.

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Banks handle these releases differently, and while some are immediate, others may process it as a temporary charge that is then refunded. The reversal can take up to *30 days* to complete, as pending authorisations typically expire after that time on banks end.

Unfortunately, we don't have full visibility into all the parties involved in the payment processing beyond our payment partner. Therefore, we can't track the exact status of the preauthorisation release once it has been sent.

*Changes suggested:*

1. Mandatory Disclosure (Add notice requirement)

Change: Require the Receiving Party to notify Bolt before disclosing confidential info when legally compelled.

Why: Without notice, Bolt loses the chance to protect or limit disclosure through legal means.

# Liability / Damages (Limit to direct damages)

Change: Remove liability for “indirect damages” and limit claims to direct losses only.

Why: Indirect damages are unpredictable and potentially massive; this keeps exposure reasonable and proportionate.

# Injunctive Relief (Added a clause)

Change: Add a clause allowing Bolt to seek injunctions if confidential info is at risk of disclosure.

Why: Money damages may not be enough. Injunctions allow Bolt to stop disclosure quickly and protect sensitive info.

hello [~accountid:712020:13946812-3ac2-4bb9-b760-51af61d581a0] 01 RH_Ghana_T1 and 01 RH_Ghana_T1_Low/Moderate are assigned to both agents.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* This week 🙃 Bolt wants to deliver a competition giveaway to help boost interest in Bolt Flex in Manchester.
** Giveaway of Fifa 2026 game, available for Flex drivers from 30 Sept to 3 Oct. Winner selected at random from Manchester Flex drivers.
** Eligible drivers will be sent a push notification (and a WhatsApp will be sent to the Manchester drivers' group).
** Eligible drivers automatically participate, but can opt out by contacting a specific email address set out un the T&Cs.
** Winners will be contacted by email or telephone using the contact details on their driver account. Winners will then be announced via in-app message.
* We have been provided with a set of T&Cs ([link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pQDTYR9uY_rQRObc3Bm3K_kghqQEfZ-W/edit]).
** Clause 7 of the T&Cs deals with privacy:
*** Contains a link to the correct privacy notice.
*** By accepting the prize, the winner consents to Bolt publishing their details / image on the website. We may also need to share surname and country to people who email us, as well as the ASA. Winner can object to certain details being published, except for first name and surname.
* *Request*: Review the T&Cs before it goes live.

+*THOUGHTS*+

* Ultimately this is very low risk, so we definitely will not block (/) 
* T&Cs explain that the winner is chosen at random, so this satisfies fairness requirements (/) 
* This is covered from a transparency POV (/) 
** Data at-issue is driver name, phone number, email address, city, account status (i.e., Bolt Flex) and image. Account status is not explicitly included in the relevant row, but this is minor and is included in the T&Cs, so we can consider this as covered.
** Purpose is marketing / facilitating participation in a giveaway.
** Legal basis should be legitimate interest (eligibility criteria) [NB. not CN, as hard to argue with auto-enrolment - backed-up by clause 3.5 which allows drivers to opt out of the giveaway], CN (announcing the winner - hint at consent as well), and legitimate interest / legal obligation (sharing with third parties).
** No need to include additional language on recipients, transfers, rights etc. However, probably worth including something on retention 💡 as we should not be retaining data for any longer than is necessary.
* Legal basis for publishing details is a bit problematic (!) 
** Based on Clause 7.2, this is consent. However, driver can only object in advance of 4 October, and even then, cannot object to name being posted. Consent is not a halfway house - if the driver withdraws their consent, then we have to remove the lot.
** We ordinarily rely on CN to announce winner. I would suggest taking the same approach here. CN as the legal basis for announcing name, and hint at consent if needed  💡
* It is also unclear why exactly we need to share the winner’s details with anyone who emails us (see Clause 7.3).
** From quick research, CAP Code Rule 8.28.5 expects promoters to: (i) make the surname and country of major prize winners available; (ii) provide an opt-out before entry; and (iii) keep details to supply to ASA ([link|https://www.asa.org.uk/type/non_broadcast/code_section/08.html]). Fine.
*** NB. ‘Making available’ includes sending it out on request, so actually Clause 7.3 is fine.
** However, ideally no objection window - this is not time-limited 💡 
* Other issues:
** Automatic opt-in - Although not ideal, ultimately low risk. Also, in T&Cs it says the drivers can opt-out, so this is ok (/) 
** Push notification - We would be able to rely on soft opt-in here. Processes should already be in place to object (/) 
*** WhatsApp channel already exists, so usual privacy risks apply. Ideally, we want to avoid posting any marketing comms on the channel (see [+LSS-54700+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-54700]), but ultimately this is low risk, particularly as it is not third-party marketing (/) 
** Contacting the winners - This is fine, and based on CN. Not explicitly spelled out in the T&Cs, but this is relatively logical and should not pose an issue.
** Announcing the winner - This is fine. We can rely on CN for channels (e.g., in-app), and it is set out in the T&Cs that info will be published. Ultimately low risk.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Amend the T&Cs per the above, and advise that: (i) the data should only be retained for 6 months; and (ii) we should not be time-limiting objection.

The ride waybill is NOT automatically emitted at a specific moment during the ride flow. Instead, it's generated on-demand when requested by either:
1. The driver (through the driver app)
2. Admin panel users (for support/compliance purposes)
Key Timing Constraints
The waybill can only be accessed AFTER the driver has accepted the order. Specifically:

:x: Waybill is NOT available during:
• DRIVER_BOOKING - When the driver is being matched
• WAITING_DRIVER_CONFIRMATION - When waiting for driver to accept
:white_check_mark: Waybill IS available from:
• DRIVER_ACCEPTED - *After driver accepts the order*
• DRIVER_ARRIVED_TO_CLIENT - When driver arrives at pickup
• DRIVING_WITH_CLIENT - During the ride
• ARRIVED_TO_DESTINATION - When reaching destination
• FINISHED - After ride completion
*Summary*
The waybill is emitted/generated on-demand starting from the moment the driver accepts the order, not at any specific automatic trigger point in the ride flow. It becomes accessible as soon as the order state moves beyond the pre-acceptance states and remains available throughout and after the ride completion.

*_Risk assessments_*_: what are the requirements to perform risk assessments? Is a generic assessment based on the role (e.g. Mechanic) and working environment (e.g. warehouse) sufficient or is a site and location specific assessment required? Does the risk assessment need to be conducted in person? How long is the risk assessment valid for?_

_The Code envisages two types of assessments: (i) assessment of workplaces and (ii) assessment of employees._

*_Assessment of workplaces_*

_According to the Code, the employer is required to conduct assessment of workplaces in order to (i) ensure the provision of occupational safety measures in the relevant workplaces, (ii) determine and improve the state of production sanitation and hygiene, (iii) increase labour productivity and work efficiency. Assessment of workplaces shall also be conducted while the introduction of the most advanced methods of labour organization, including the application of new equipment or technology. A workplace assessment commission consisting of representatives of trade unions, occupational safety services and professional experts on labour organization shall be established for the purposes of assessment._

_The “Rules of assessment of workplaces” approved by the Decision of the Cabinet of Ministers No. 38 dated 06 March 2000 (the “Rules”) determines the objectives of the assessment of workplaces, the procedure of its conduct and the rules for the use and formalization of the results of the assessment in enterprises. As per the Rules, the time of the assessment is determined by the enterprise itself, depending on changes in the nature and conditions of the labour, but in any event no less than once every 5 years (ordinary assessment). Assessment of workplaces shall also be conducted in connection with (i) the replacement of production equipment, (ii) change of technological processes, (iii) restructuring of collective protection means, as well as (iv) for the purpose of eliminating the violations identified at the time of assessment of workplace on working conditions conducted by the State Labor Inspection Service (extra-ordinary assessment)._

*_Assessment of employees_*

_The Code provides that all employees may, at the employer’s discretion, be subjected to assessment (except for certain types of employees specifically excluded by the Code from assessment, such as pregnant women, employees under the age of 18, etc.) conducted by the assessment commission in person in order to (i) verify the level of professionalism of the employees, (ii) identify their suitability for the position (profession) they occupy according to their qualifications and skills._ 

_It is further provided that only employees who have been working at the relevant workplace for at least one year may undergo assessment. Each employee may be subjected to assessment no more than once every three years, and scientific workers no more than once every five years._

Since the fleet company is currently in liquidation and officially listed as having no active establishment, we cannot accept a simple unilateral request from the fleet owner to change the company’s banking details.

Under French law, once a company enters liquidation proceedings, only the court-appointed liquidator (“liquidateur judiciaire”) has authority to represent the company and manage its affairs, including financial matters such as bank accounts. If the person claims to be acting as their own liquidator, this would only be legally possible if they were formally appointed as such in the liquidation judgment. In that case, *they must provide the official court decision appointing them liquidator, not a modified Kbis extract.*

A manually altered Kbis is fraudulent and cannot be considered valid.

 Please let me know if you need any further support.

I checked the 48V1/2 outputs overcurrent triggering logic:

* If there is a short circuit for a “short moment”, then the output is turned off, the 48V output error is set active. If the short occurred for short time, then the output is restored and the error bit is set back to 0. If 3 overcurrent events happen, then the error is latched and the error bit is active until:
*# Controller power cycle
*# Restart command is sent to the controller by CAN.
*# The error bit is written to 0 by CAN command
* The overcurrent error is also triggered, when the output is set to SC and is kept for long time. In this case, 3 consecutive tries are not necessary.

Controller 48V output testing can be seen below:

The 48V2 output (Black line on graph) drops to 0  when short circuit is detected and the error bit (blue line) is set to 1 until the error is cleared. After 3 consecutive SC events, the output is turned OFF until reset.

Graph 1: Values reported from controller on CAN bus, on this graph, the 48V2 output is shorted 3 times “quickly”.

!image-20250930-090335.png|width=1244,height=720,alt="image-20250930-090335.png"!

Graph 2: 48V output behavior measured on 48V output, measured in sync with graph 1.

!image-20250930-091207.png|width=5712,height=4284,alt="image-20250930-091207.png"!

Graph 3: 1 “long” short circuit which triggers the error bit to 1 continuously. On this graph, the 48V2 output is short circuited continuously. 

!image-20250930-092253.png|width=1246,height=724,alt="image-20250930-092253.png"!

*Conclusion:*

# The Output may spark in case of SC event, but the output is actually turned off.
## The output is off after 3 “short” time period SC events or after 1 “long” time period SC event.
# The controller does not actually measure 48V1/2 voltages, the voltage is estimated from battery input voltage to the controller.
## It would make sense to add voltage measurement to 48V1/2 outputs for the following reasons:
###  To detect broken mosfet (Mosfet open or short circuit), which drives the 48V output.
### It would help to debug/detect anomalies with devices on 48V.
# The current measurement is quite noisy, it should be checked whether it can be improved.

Investigating the situation regarding the SAF-T file. The main problem persists: the file continues to show errors, *and there has been no response from support.*

Upon reviewing the SAF-T, I have identified a critical issue with users’ fiscal numbers. In several cases, invalid entries such as phone numbers, postal codes, or other random numbers are being accepted as valid tax IDs. This indicates that *there is no validation or format check* in place to prevent incorrect data from being entered.

The consequence is that when correct tax IDs are used, invoices are generated properly. However, when invalid numbers are entered, the system produces poor or incorrect invoices. This issue is not limited to locals—non-local users are also affected, and the system still accepts invalid formats including phone numbers with country codes.

As a temporary workaround, it would be better to allow issuing invoices as *“final consumer”* when the rental contract contains the correct ID and driving license information, rather than accepting invalid tax IDs.

*This issue requires urgent attention, as it directly affects the integrity of the invoices and the SAF-T reporting.*

Mūsų atsiųstas atsakymas jiems į pirminę užklausą: 

Sveiki, Kazy,

Grįžtu prie esamo klausimo. Gavau komentarus iš teisininkų:



* pakeisti 2.4 punktą ir išdėstyti jį nauja redakcija taip:
"2.4. Klientas atlieka mokėjimą pagal sąskaitą faktūrą per *30* dienų nuo sąskaitos faktūros gavimo datos. Negavus mokėjimo iki nustatyto termino, visos vartotojo užklausos dėl “Bolt” paslaugų naudojimo bus atmetamos. *Sąskaitoje faktūroje privalo būti įrašytas Kliento iš anksto nurodytas PO numeris*."



* papildyti 3 ir 4 skyriais:



# *Etika*



3.1.Šalys pareiškia, kad jos vykdo veiklą laikydamosi  galiojančių įstatymų ir poįstatyminių teisės aktų bei aukščiausių etikos standartų. Šalys ypač netoleruoja korupcijos. Bolt veikla turi būti suderinama su PwC Globaliame trečiųjų šalių etikos kodekse, patalpintame PwC globalioje svetainėje, adresu [https://www.pwc.com/gx/en/about/ethics-business-conduct/global-third-party-code-of-conduct.html|https://www.pwc.com/gx/en/about/ethics-business-conduct/global-third-party-code-of-conduct.html|smart-link] , įtvirtintomis vertybėmis ir principais. Bet kokie Bolt veiksmai ar neveikimas, priešingi aukščiau šiame punkte nurodytiems pareiškimams ir reikalavimams, laikytini esminiu Sutarties pažeidimu.



*Atsakymas:* 2.4 punkto ir 3. punkto pridėjimas - sutinkame.



4.1. Šalys susitaria papildyti 1.3. dalį sakiniu:



"_Apie konkrečius Paslaugų teikimo sąlygų pasikeitimus Bolt turi pranešti Klientui raštu 14 dienų prieš įsigaliojant pakeitimams_".



*Atsakymas:* 1.3 dalyje pakeitimai negali būti atliekami, nes ši dalis apibrėžia „Bolt Business“ platformos formą, o paslaugų teikimo sąlygos taikomos individualiems vartotojams, kurie su bendrosiomis sąlygomis sutinka asmeniškai. Tuo remiantis, galime atnaujinti 8.2 punktą su sąlyga, kad apie Jums aktualius „Bolt Business“ bendrųjų sąlygų pakeitimus būsite informuoti ne vėliau kaip prieš 14 kalendorinių dienų iki jų įsigaliojimo.





4.2. Šalys sutinka pakeisti 3.2. dalį ir išdėstyti ją nauja redakcija taip:

 

"3.2 Klientas sutinka atlyginti tiesiogines „Bolt“ išlaidas ar žalą, patirtas dėl Vartotojo naudojimosi „Bolt“ paslaugomis arba dėl galiojančių įstatymų pažeidimo."



*Atsakymas*: Kadangi „Bolt“ paslaugomis naudotojai naudojasi Kliento interesais, o naudotojus prideda ar pašalina pats Klientas, natūralu, kad Klientas taip pat įsipareigoja atlyginti bet kokią naudotojo padarytą žalą ar kitokias išimtines išlaidas, patirtas naudojantis „Bolt“ paslaugomis.





4.3. Šalys sutinka pakeisti 6.2. dalį ir išdėstyti ją nauja redakcija taip:





"6.2. Bendra „Bolt“ atsakomybė už visus reikalavimus, kylančius pagal Sutartį arba susijusius su ja per vienerius kalendorinius metus, nesvarbu, ar tai

būtų sutartiniai, deliktiniai, ar kitokie reikalavimai, neviršija dvigubos sumos, kurią Klientas sumokėjo „Bolt“ pagal Sutartį per vienerių kalendorinių metų laikotarpį iki pirmojo reikalavimo atsiradimo dienos."



*Atsakymas*: 

Šis punktas yra kertinis, todėl privalo išlikti toks koks yra ir negali būti koreguojamas. „Bolt Business“ ir „Bolt“ paslaugos teikiamos principu „kaip yra“ ir „kaip prieinama“. „Bolt“ negarantuoja, kad prieiga bus nenutrūkstama ar be klaidų. Nors mes dedame visas pastangas, kad maksimaliai užtikrintume Kliento pasitenkinimą mūsų paslaugomis, Jūs liekate laisvi naudotis konkurentų paslaugomis ir bet kuriuo metu galite nustoti naudotis „Bolt“ paslaugomis be jokių sankcijų.



4.4. Šalys susitaria pakeisti 6.5. dalį ir išdėstyti ją nauja redakcija taip:



"6.5. Šalys gali naudoti arba nurodyti kitos šalies pavadinimą, logotipą, prekių ženklus ar paslaugų ženklus pranešime spaudai ar kitu būdu tik gavę išankstinį

tokios kitos šalies sutikimą kiekvienu atskiru atveju." 



*Atsakymas*: Bolt Business bendrųjų sąlygų ir nuostatų 6.5 punktas patikslinamas ir išdėstomas taip:

 

“Kiekviena šalis, kiekvienu atveju, gavusi išankstinį kitos šalies sutikimą, gali naudoti arba nurodyti kitos šalies pavadinimą, logotipą, prekių ar paslaugų ženklus pranešime spaudai ar kitaip. Klientas turi laikytis „Bolt“ prekės ženklo gairių.”



4.5. Šalys susitaria netaikyti 8.2. Dalies.



*Atsakymas*:  Atsižvelgdami į Jūsų pastabas, galime sutikti su 8.2 punkto atnaujinimu. Atnaujintas punktas atrodytų taip:

„Bolt“ pasilieka teisę bet kuriuo metu keisti šias Bendrąsias sąlygas. Tokie pakeitimai įsigalioja po to, kai jie buvo pateikti Klientui per Verslo portalą arba apie juos buvo pranešta Klientui, nurodant kontaktinius duomenis, įregistruotus Verslo portale, per protingą laikotarpį iki pakeitimų įsigaliojimo, kuris yra ne trumpesnis kaip 14 dienų nuo pranešimo, išskyrus atvejus, kai:

* _„Bolt“ turi teisinę ar reguliavimo prievolę, pagal kurią ji privalo pakeisti šias Bendrąsias sąlygas taip, kad negalėtų laikytis išankstinio pranešimo termino;_
* _reikia nedelsiant atlikti pakeitimus, kad būtų išvengta nenumatytos ir neišvengiamos grėsmės, susijusios su sveikatos, saugos ar kibernetinio saugumo rizika, arba kad būtų apsaugota „Bolt“ platforma ar jos naudotojai nuo sukčiavimo, kenkėjiškų programų, šlamšto ar duomenų pažeidimų;_
* _Klientas nusprendė atsisakyti išankstinio pranešimo laikotarpio; arba_

h3. On a separate note, I would like to flag key risks related to implementing dual unsubscribe mechanism:

*Inconsistency in Unsubscribe Mechanisms (High Risk if discovered)*

# Two different unsubscribe flows would exist: in high-risk markets (EU/UK/CH), users can opt out of all marketing at once, while in other markets unsubscribe applies only to a single category.
# This structural inconsistency could be noticed by:
#* *Users with multiple profiles across countries* (e.g., one EU account and one non-EU account) who may perceive the difference as unfair and misleading and report Bolt to authorities.
#* *Regulators during audits or investigations*, who could question why Bolt, as an EU company, does not apply GDPR-level standards globally.
# If discovered, particularly in the EU, regulators could frame this as a *fairness breach* (failure to respect the right to object to direct marketing in a consistent and fair way).
# This could lead to corrective orders, reputational harm, and potentially *fines up to 4% of annual global turnover under GDPR*. Realistically, fines for this type of issue would likely be lower, but could still reach *millions of euros in larger EU countries*.
# The *probability of escalation is not high*, but the *potential impact is high*, which makes this a material compliance risk.

*User Expectations in Non-High-Risk Countries (Medium Risk)*

* Users in non-high-risk jurisdictions will still generally expect that “unsubscribe” means no more marketing at all.
* Under the category-based unsubscribe approach, they may continue to receive other marketing messages, which could trigger complaints.
* This risk is *lower* than in the EU/UK/CH because:
** other unsubscribe options exist (in-app, customer support), and
** regulators in these countries tend to act only where complaint volumes are significant.
* Nonetheless, the risk is *still present* and could escalate if user complaints increase or if global regulators begin adopting stricter EU-style standards.

The list is grouped by {{user}} and {{<schema_name.table_name>}}. The included columns are:

* *cluster*. Database cluster
* *hostgroup*. Database cluster ID
* *type*. Database management system [mysql, tidb]
* *collected_at*. Collection [+time.time()+|https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.time]
* *collected_from.* The PRIMARY database server of the cluster.
* *env*. Environment [prelive, live]
* *user*. Database username
* *table_schema*. The database and table which the user can access, are separated by “.” {{<schema_name.table_name>}}
Where *** means access to all databases and/or all tables.
* *privilege_type*. List of privileges that the user has granted. Between ““, separated by coma.
* *grant_priv*. Does the user have grant privileges {{[Y/N]}}, Having GRANT privilege means it can give PRIVILEGES to other users, and themselves.
* *locked*. Is the user locked {{[Y/N]}} a Locked user cannot establish a connection to the databases.
* *created_at*. Created date for users created by configless.

I understand that introducing a fleet owner category in fleet-documents would require significant effort. However, I have concerns about moving documents from fleet company to fleet owners as it might actually create a new set of serious challenges rather than resolve the existing ones.

What we currently have under category is often a mix of company-level and manager-level documents. Switching from storing documents on the company entity to storing them on the manager entity definitely improves our compliance by ensuring all managers have the necessary documents, but we risk replicating the same structural problems we’re attempting to move away from.

• Many company-wide documents (e.g. bank statement) are not tied to any single fleet manager. Moving such documents from company to manager creates a situation very similar to the way vehicle documents were historically stored on driver profiles (and in some markets still are, until migration is fully complete). It breaks the logical ownership of documents and opens the door to significant operational inefficiencies. 
• In companies with multiple managers, the same company document would need to be uploaded to each manager’s profile. That means ops would process the same file several times, deal with redundant copies, and face simultaneous expiry events when those duplicates come due for renewal. This amplifies workload instead of reducing it, and introduces data integrity risks if not all copies are updated correctly. 
I might be misunderstanding your proposed solution, so please correct me if my reasoning went in a completely random direction :pray::skin-tone-3:

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Banks handle these releases differently, and while some are immediate, others may process it as a temporary charge that is then refunded.
