*Update 06/10*

*Result of CLS experiment:*
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6895665908/2025-08+Romania+Meta+Android+Conversion+Lift+Study|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6895665908/2025-08+Romania+Meta+Android+Conversion+Lift+Study|smart-link]: *No Incrementality.* Despite a daily spend of approximately €50, the experiment did not produce a statistically significant lift in signups. The spend is too little to have any impact. 

*Results of in-house experiments:*

[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6847561810/2025-08+Brussels+Google+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6847561810/2025-08+Brussels+Google+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *Incrementality.* Increase by €825 daily for Google iOS resulted in an increment of 60 statistically significant signups. The GMV to cost ratio of 4.74, which is significantly better than the target of 1.93. Incrementality was observed pretty much throughout the experiment duration, which is supported by the probability of impact of 100%.
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6885311509/2025-08+Zagreb+TikTok+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6885311509/2025-08+Zagreb+TikTok+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *No Incrementality.* With an increase of €529 daily, we did not see a statistically significant increase in signups. This was a retest of the [+experiment performed in Q2+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6338674843], which was almost incremental with similar spend levels.
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6886917021/2025-08+Germany+Meta+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6886917021/2025-08+Germany+Meta+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *No Incrementality.* An increase of €1,077 daily did not lead to a statistically significant uplift in signups. This was the first experiment on Facebook iOS in Germany.
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874792426/2025-08+Oslo+TikTok+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874792426/2025-08+Oslo+TikTok+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *No incrementality.* An increase of €1,207 daily for TikTok iOS did not result in incrementality. The spend increase was not consistent, as a result, the average daily spend was €1.2k compared to the budget of €2k daily. Some incrementality was observed towards the end of the experiment when the spends increased, which suggests we might have seen a greater effect with a consistent daily spend of approximately €2k.
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6846972267/2025-08+Paris+Meta+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6846972267/2025-08+Paris+Meta+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *Incrementality.* An increase of €3217 daily for Meta iOS resulted in an increment of 183 statistically significant signups. The GMV to cost ratio of 6.64, exceeds the target of 4.27. This is the first experiment run on Meta iOS (and the second iOS experiment overall).
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874563380/2025-08+Asunci+n+Google+Android+Decrease|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874563380/2025-08+Asunci+n+Google+Android+Decrease|smart-link]:*Incrementality*. A decrease of €1,686 daily led to a statistically significant decline of 108 signups daily with a probability of impact of 100%. This suggests that there is incrementality at daily spends of ~€2.3k, however, the MMM suggested spend for Q4 is €50 as it takes into account multiple non-incremental experiments in the past. 
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874628798/2025-08+Zurich+Google+iOS+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6874628798/2025-08+Zurich+Google+iOS+Increase|smart-link]: *Inconclusive.* Even though the result of the experiment shows that an increase of €971 daily for Google iOS resulted in an increase of 35 signups daily with a probability of impact of 95%. However, upon checking the daily trend, we see that the first half of the experiment did not see any incrementality, and the signups suddenly shot up after 25th August. Upon checking further, we see that this increase in signups is purely driven by tourists. Signups likely surged because Weltklasse Zürich (athletics final on 27–28 Aug) and Zürich Openair (music festival on 29–30 Aug) brought in large amount of tourists. Keeping this in mind, the experiment has been marked as inconclusive as the increase in signups is because of external events. The recommendation is to retest the experiment at a later date.
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6846612277/2025-08+Kenya+TikTok+Android+Increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6846612277/2025-08+Kenya+TikTok+Android+Increase|smart-link]: *Incrementality.* An increase of €957 daily for TikTok Android led to a statistically significant uplift of 625 daily signups. The CPA is only €4 and the GMV to cost ratio of 10 far exceeds the target of 3.42. Nairobi hosted multiple [+CHAN 2025+|https://pashawise.com/chan-2025-fixtures/] (African Nations Championship) football matches in the month of August, which coincides with the experiment dates and might explain the increased signups. However, these signups were coming from local users, and not tourists. Given this context, the experiment can be considered as incremental, however, a re-test with the same tactic at a later date is recommended.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* *Deadline* = 7 October 2025 🕓 
** Unfortunately was not raised to me until 2 October :melting_face: 
* On 7 September, a non-user (Stephen- apparently country is South Africa -  email is [kingambrose@gmail.com|mailto:kingambrose@gmail.com]) emailed Bolt ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/643242675]) claiming that their email address was being used in an unauthorised manner (as they were receiving emails from Bolt without ever signing up for Bolt services). Non-user claims this is a clear breach of the GDPR. They request the following, and are threatening to escalate this to the Irish DPC:
** {color:#403294}*Removal of their email address from Bolt’s systems under A17 GDPR;*{color}
** {color:#403294}*Confirmation that their email address has been blocked from being re-added.*{color}
** {color:#403294}*Disclosure of what personal data Bolt holds in relation to their email address, and the source.*{color}
** {color:#403294}*Reference number for this complaint.*{color}
* *Acknowledgement sent* on 8 September ✅  [+DSR-1816+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/DSR-1816] was raised on the same day.
** Unfortunately, Emilia did not pick this up until 1 October - it seems that the DSAR element was missed.
* Based on investigation by CS, 3 rider profiles found with the same email ([here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/280226883/overview], [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/133003587/overview] and [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/232985268/overview])
** It appears that on 9 September, email address was removed from all such profiles, such that it no longer appears on any (see [here|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/search?tz=Europe%2FTallinn&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22email_prefix%22%3A%22kingambrose%40gmail.com%22%7D%7D]). Same for drivers.
** Unfortunately, CS’s initial response was to ask for the non-user’s account information… this incensed the non-user further. They have therefore also requested {color:#403294}*confirmation of what steps Bolt will take to prevent further unauthorised use*{color}.
* On 9 September, CS wrote to the non-user confirming that another user had added the email address to their account. CS (thankfully) referred the non-user to the [blocking web form|https://bolt.eu/en/email-report/], and flagged this would result in deletion.
** However, the non-user continued to insist that they wanted a complaint reference number. Non-user claimed they had previously filled in the webpage twice in 2024.
* On 25 September, the non-user picked up this issue again on this thread, claiming they were still receiving “_emails … coming from_ [_bolt.eu_|http://bolt.eu]_, … includ[ing] marketing and taxi receipts_”. The non-user says they will provide screenshots for “_1000 EUR per screen shot_” 😂 
** Non-user has also separately said they will charge EUR 5000 per email from Bolt ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/442714261]), so they are clearly just being unreasonable.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Data Breach:
** Although non-user refuses to provide proof, it is likely that some personal data breach did occur here, given that the email was used across multiple accounts. As such, this should be reported to the ODPO (done [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C0678KJ49UH/p1759482577716499]).
** In any case, this looks very unlikely to be reportable ✅ 
* DSAR:
** Removal of email from Bolt’s systems - We have deleted the email address from user accounts. However, we need to retain a copy in the blocker tool (to prevent further misuse) and we have a copy based our comms with the user (for CS / defending legal claims).
** Blocking confirmation - We should be able to confirm this. If user continues to get emails, they should provide us screenshots - we cannot help them if they will not help us. Otherwise, we can assume they are lying.
** Disclosure of data held - Given deletion, we retain their email address in the blocker and the email comms with the user. Source was when it was originally added to user profiles (we cannot share their identities - likely an honest mistake), as well as when the non-user added it to the tool.
** Reference number - We can provide the Beehive thread number if the non-user continues to complain.
* Other:
** Registered in Cognito ([link|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/datasubjectrightsrequeststracker/1-all-entries/1982]).

Dear Stephen,

Thank you for flagging the issue that you have been receiving emails to [kingambrose@gmail.com|mailto:kingambrose@gmail.com] (the “*Email Address*”) despite not setting up a Bolt account, as well as your data subject rights request that we received on 7 September 2025 (the “*Request*”).

As noted in previous correspondence, we investigated this issue internally and identified other Bolt users who had listed your Email Address on their own accounts. The Email Address has now been removed from these accounts, and so you should no longer receive any emails from Bolt in this context. Please note that we have not seen any evidence to suggest that this was the result of potentially fraudulent activity. Instead, it seems that other individuals mistakenly listed your Email Address on their accounts. In situations like this, using an email address that is more distinctive and personal - such as one that includes your full name or another unique identifier - can help prevent confusion and reduce the likelihood of similar incidents in the future. You can also report any instances of suspected email abuse through [https://bolt.eu/en/email-report/|https://bolt.eu/en/email-report/]. Please ensure that you have deleted any unrecognised emails that you previously received from Bolt. If you continue to receive any emails of this nature, we would be grateful if you could send us screenshots so that our team can assist with resolving the matter.

We have included your Email Address on our email misuse feature (the “*Feature*”) to ensure that it cannot be listed on any Bolt passenger accounts in future. Please therefore note the following in response to your Request:

* Although we have removed your Email Address from the user accounts that we identified, we will continue to store a copy of your Email Address on the Feature for the purpose of preventing email misuse. We also retain a copy of your communications made with Bolt via this Email Address (i.e., your emails that brought this issue to our attention), for the purpose of investigating, exercising and defending claims.
* As noted above, the source of this issue was that other Bolt users listed your Email Address on their own accounts. We are unable to disclose information that reveals the identities of these individuals, as doing so would threaten their rights and freedoms in accordance with Article 15(4) of the GDPR.
* An internal reference number for this thread is # 643242675.

We trust that this addresses your concerns. If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

*SUMMARY OF RISK ANALYSIS* 

+Summary of current position in Ireland+

* Driver Score UX is live in IE (robo blocking was previously turned off). 
* In the UK (under the Principal Model), this model is already reclassified to worker status, but introducing monitoring of driver behaviour (whether human or automated) could increase the risk of drivers being seen as workers for the entire time they are online rather than just while in the app. Legal strongly recommends we do not proceed unless UK Ops sign this off. With regards to the *UK Agency Model*, this would be an absolute no go. Any driver monitoring here would significantly undermine the model and the project as a whole.
* In *Ireland,*  the model has not yet been reclassified and this step could tip it over into reclassification. 

+Summary of proposed changes in Ireland+

* Central Ops want to implement the human review so that the local team has possibilities to suspend drivers short term (14 days) if metrics are down.
* The rationale for this is that due to the increased reclassification risk over the years and [+Platform Work Directive+|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_Work_Directive] (PWD) regulating the platform work providers (such as Bolt) - there was a need to put in place (_as per Article 8_) a human review process for significant decisions, including a right to an explanation of any decision from an automated system, and reasons for restricting access to an account (as per this note: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link]). 
* Local Legal and Local Ops can decide which metrics can be considered for IE. 
* Human suspension reviews will be performed by a dedicated global team of outsourced agents (here is a document setting out the human suspension review guidelines for the external agents: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei|smart-link] 
* A full catalogue with triggers and screenshots for Local Ops can be found here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link] 
* More context can be found here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link]  

+Legal Analysis+ 

_Platform Work Directive_ 

* After a prolonged and controversial journey through the EU legislative process, on 11 November 2024 the Directive on improving working conditions in platform work (“Platform Work Directive”) was published in the Official Journal. EU member states will have until 2 December 2026 to transpose its provisions into national law. 
* The Platform Work Directive requires digital labour platforms to subject their algorithmic management systems to human oversight and review.  Suspensions, dismissals, or equally significant decisions must be taken by a human in light of the potential for discrimination. 
* In preparation for the implementation of the Platform Work Directive, employers should pre-emptively address forthcoming obligations related to algorithmic oversight by ensuring there is human oversight when using automated systems particularly in higher risk circumstances.

_Reclassification Risk_ 

* As mentioned above, Ireland is not as “high risk” compared with the UK. However, it is “medium risk” meaning regulators may probe and unions could test cases - driver suspension could tip Ireland into a higher reclassification risk and we want to avoid that. 
* Reclassification risk is not caused by human review per se, but by the choice of metrics used to trigger suspension. 
* From a review of the documents provided by Central Ops, my *concern is around suspensions due to low acceptance rates, cancellations and car quality:* these look like KPIs and employment-style oversight and resemble performance management. 
* Lower risk categories include suspensions in the event of safety, fraud or serious misconduct as these can be defensible as consumer protection measures. 
* We need to ensure that driver-facing comms are watertight and give explicit reasons and explanation rights for any suspensions, and clear guidance as to the appeals procedure. 
* Notwithstanding the above, the Ireland T&Cs also only give the right to suspend/terminate drivers in the event of suspected illegal activity, fraudulent activity or significant complaints - [https://bolt.eu/en-ie/legal/terms-for-drivers-2025/|https://bolt.eu/en-ie/legal/terms-for-drivers-2025/|smart-link]. 

_Conclusion_ 

Human Review is mandatory for Platform Work Directive compliance; although it takes effect from December 2026, it is prudent for the business to start pre-emptively aligning with it. Proceeding in Ireland reduces legal exposure compared to automation. However, expanding suspensions to *low acceptance rates/cancellations/car quality* *materially increases reclassification risk*. My recommendation is that we do not proceed on suspensions related to any reason *other than safety, fraud, serious misconduct.*

*Driver Score Human Review - Ireland* 

Hi [~accountid:6332c7ab409249995ee9c5e8], I have reviewed the materials provided by Central Ops in relation to the proposed Human Review for Driver Score suspensions and have carried out a review of the reclassification risks (please see below). 

+High-Level Summary+

* *HIGH RISK: Strong recommendation to proceed with caution*, for the following reasons: 
** In the UK, regulators have already *reclassified drivers as “workers”* under the Principal Model. 
** In Ireland, our model is based on the Agency model and drivers have *not yet been reclassified*. *Driver suspension could tip Ireland into a higher reclassification risk and we want to avoid this*.
* If, upon review, you are comfortable with driver score suspensions (with Human Review) in Ireland, Legal recommends that we limit this to *suspensions relating to safety, fraud and serious misconduct only.* 
* Suspensions for *any other reasons (i.e. cancellations or car quality)* would *significantly increase the risk of drivers being reclassified as workers*. We do not want to be seen to be exercising control of _how_ drivers can provide their services or _when_ they can work.  

+Risk Matrix based on examples provided in the+ [+Human Review Guidelines+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei]

||*Category*||*Reclassification Risk Level*||*Commentary*||
|Safety/Serious Misconduct/Fraud|🟢 *Low*|Strongest justification if Ops decides to proceed with suspensions. Suspending for these reasons are also in line with our driver T&Cs.|
|Cancellations (before or at pickup)|🟠 *Medium–High*|Can look like control of working patterns. T&Cs do not cover this.|
|Low Rider Ratings / “Bad Behaviour”|🟠 *Medium–High*|Risk of perceived disciplinary use of ratings (i.e. controlling driver behaviour) - increased reclassification risk.|
|Car Quality|🟠 *Medium–High*|Can be seen as managing “tools of trade”.|
|Generic Rider Complaints|🔴 *High*|Highly subjective and can be viewed as controlling driver behaviour.|
|Low Acceptance Rate|🔴 *Very* *High*|KPI-based control which may resemble employee performance management.|

+Summary of proposed changes in Ireland+

* Driver Score UX is already live in Ireland, but *no suspensions* are currently applied.
* Central Ops want to implement the human review so that the local team has the option to suspend drivers short term (14 days) if metrics are down.
* The rationale for this is that due to the increased reclassification risk over the years and [+Platform Work Directive+|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_Work_Directive] (PWD) regulating the platform work providers (such as Bolt) - there was a need to put in place (_as per Article 8_) a human review process for significant decisions, including a right to an explanation of any decision from an automated system, and reasons for restricting access to an account (as per this note: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link]).
* Local Legal and Local Ops can decide which metrics can be considered for IE. 
* Human suspension reviews will be performed by a dedicated global team of outsourced agents (here is a document setting out the human suspension review guidelines for the external agents: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei|smart-link]
* A full catalogue with triggers and screenshots for Local Ops can be found here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link]
* More context can be found here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/6852444686/Manual+Review+for+Driver+Score+suspensions|smart-link]

+Next Steps+

* As highlighted above, this initiative is *HIGH RISK for Ireland* and we recommend proceeding with caution. 
* If you are comfortable with proceeding with Driver Score suspensions (with Human Review), please review the metrics carefully in the [+Human Review Guidelines+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei] and decide which metrics and country specifics need to be considered for Ireland - *NOTE:* 
** as mentioned above, we recommend applying suspensions only for *safety, fraud and serious misconduct*;
** for all other signals (ratings, car quality, rider complaints), we recommend adopting a mandatory “always override” logic that mirrors the approach used in Portugal, Belgium, Netherlands and Switzerland, as set out in the [+Human Review Guidelines+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q3OC64ofJa0Yp_RJc1nATYcmxn5jvY4Xs0fZ6Q8YQcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.w1cqzmiuohei]. 

Please also feel free to loop in the rest of the team as needed. 

Best wishes

Implementation details:
This task is going to affect calculated balances as well. The aim is to introduce one queue for calculations and recalculations. What should be done:
1. Whenever there is a need we should create a calculation task that holds info about the date calculation should start from, end at, aim of it (finalize(for eod and history)/calculate(for intraday)) and status (waiting, processing, done), account and timezone
2. When task is created we should also create a recalculation queue that will correspond to this task: these tasks should a have a status as well, date, link to parent task
3. There should also be a cron that picks up tasks, find the queue and starts processing it. Aim of tasks should be propagated to executor. It should turn all balances between start and end date to calculating status and the perform needed action 
4. Intraday calculation tasks should be created upon receiving a scheduler signal
5. When receiving an eod event, calculation should be performed synchronously and sent forward
6. Cron should run frequently (every ~0.5-1 min) and pick up calculation tasks immediately, for finalization tasks it should have some kind of a delay (like 10-15 mins after task creation to allow txs to come through in case there’re multiple changed txs)

I have looked into the case and investigated what happened. 
There are a couple quite interesting interactions here. 

1. This is a reuse booking order. The first order was cancelled, but Bolt reused the funds for another order. 
First cancelled order [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/2147090569/575?orderTryId=2684194372|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/2147090569/575?orderTryId=2684194372]


!image-20251003-073927.png|width=704,height=593!

The payment was used for a second order the same day. 
Order was cancelled, but customer was charged the cancellation fee 60 SEK [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/2147091772/575?orderTryId=2684195898|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/2147091772/575?orderTryId=2684195898]

2. This was a partial capture meaning that the authorized funds were higher than the captured amount. 
When this happens Bolt sends a void authorization for the remaining amount. 
In this case the authorization was 118 SEK and Capture for 60 SEK. We voided the authorization for 58 SEK on 28th of September. 

We have noticed that some banks are not able to correctly parse the void authorization message and are linking it to the capture. Meaning that the information is displayed to the customer incorrectly. We did not charge the customer for 60 SEK, but returned 58 SEK instead. 
Here is a payment timeline from the CheckOut portal to help to visualize what happened. Please do not share the screenshot with the customer. 


!image-20251003-074303.png|width=555,height=414!

We would suggest the customer to check with their bank about the “Charge” of 60 SEK. You can provide them the ARN {{524144660718}} to locate the authorization release of 58 SEK. 

Let me know if you have any questions.

*Limitations*

{quote}_“Amendments of the Articles of Incorporation (including but not limited to change in the number of directors) and the By-Laws are excluded and may be covered by a separate scope and fee.”_{quote}

Could you please confirm whether these documents need to be submitted to the SEC every year together with the AFS, or only when changes occur? If it is only in case of changes, then we understand this engagement does not cover such filings in future years. You assisted in the onboarding phase to file these one-time and any possible amendments to these documents in the future is the responsibility of Bolt (to inform SEC and submit to SEC the amended versions). 

*SGV/EY PH: This limitation refers to any applications for the amendment of the Articles of Incorporation and/or By-Laws of the corporation. Examples of amendments are changes in the number of directors, address, capital structure, type of shares, accounting period, officers, etc., as provided in the Articles of Incorporation or By-Laws. If there are no changes, there is necessarily no need to amend these corporate documents.*

*If there are similar changes, our team can definitely assist subject to a separate fee arrangement.*

*We also note that the submission of the General Information Sheet, or the non-tax return, which is required to be filed on an annual basis, is not included in our scope of work. Thus, we assume that this is separately handled by the corporate secretary.*

 

*Resubmission Costs*

{quote}_“Any amendment to the AFS requiring SEC resubmission will cost USD 2,000.”_{quote}

If the SEC rejects the AFS or raises queries on the filing, would this be considered an “amendment” that triggers the fee? Or what exactly does “amendment” refer to?

*SGV/EY PH: If the SEC requires re-filing due to some minor considerations, like the scanned documents does not follow the formatting,etc., there is no re-filing fee. However, if the company – for whatever reason other than minor issues like formatting – is required to re-file the AFS due to certain amendments in the AFS itself or any of its attachments like the Statement of Management Responsibility, we will be a re-filing fee.*

*Auto-renewal*
If Bolt does not provide notice before auto-renewal, would we still be charged for the new annual term even if the services are not required or used?

*SGV/EY PH: The contract term is for 12 months from the execution and the agreement is deemed renewed if no advice to terminate has been duly received. For instance, if the contract is signed on Oct. 1, 2025, it will remain effective until September 30, 2026. If Bolt does not wish to renew, SGV/EY PH must be duly notified no later than Sept. 1, 2026. Without the notice to terminate, the annual fee will still be billed regardless if the services were used.*
Could have been a case that regular payout was not generated yet and cashout was taken first on the same day.

Like we did in [other ticket |https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LEG-1076], we would like to highlight the following legal and operational considerations:

# *Legal Framework*

* Under Portuguese law, only pharmacies and MNSRM outlets that are duly registered with INFARMED may sell and deliver OTC medicines online or to customers’ homes. Being such a large group of pharmacies, we already know that _A Nossa Farmácia_ is properly licensed, but it is important to have this in mind and I think this should be verified anyway.
* The transport of medicines to the patient’s home is subject, with the necessary adaptations, to the transport rules set out in the Good Distribution Practices of medicines.
* Deliveries must be executed under the supervision of appropriately qualified personnel (pharmacists or pharmacy technicians), ensuring compliance with Good Distribution Practices (GDP) for packaging, temperature control, and security.
* Article 2(2) of _Portaria n.º 1427/2007_ requires that home delivery must be supervised by a pharmacist (for pharmacies) or a pharmacist/pharmacy technician (for OTC outlets). Article 3(3) further establishes that home delivery can only be assured by the pharmacy or the authorised point of sale where the medicine was requested.

On this basis, *our legal assessment first concluded that, strictly interpreted, delivery should be handled directly by the pharmacy or licensed outlet*—not by a third-party courier without such supervision.

That said, *we understand that there is room for interpretation: the requirement could also be understood as meaning that the pharmacist/technician must supervise the preparation, packaging, and sealing of the order* before handing it over to the courier, rather than being physically responsible for the delivery to the customer.

Both Uber and Glovo appear to operate under the interpretation that the pharmacist’s supervision at the preparation stage is sufficient.

However, it is important to note that in the [Q&A part of INFARMED website|https://www.infarmed.pt/web/infarmed/perguntas-frequentes-area-transversal/medicamentos_internet] we can read the following:

*_A farmácia pode enviar os medicamentos por correio ou estafeta?_*

_Não, a legislação determina que os medicamentos devem ser entregues ao domicílio respeitando as normas de supervisão, habilitação e formação adequada à dispensa de medicamentos e respeitar as regras de transporte previstas nas boas práticas de distribuição de medicamentos._
_As Boas Práticas de Distribuição de Medicamentos determinam:_
 _"(...) 9.4 - Os medicamentos devem ser transportados em todo o seu circuito por forma que:_
_a) Não se perca a sua identificação;_
_b) Não contaminem nem sejam contaminados por outros produtos ou materiais;_
_c) Sejam adoptadas precauções especiais contra o derrame, a rotura ou o roubo;_
_d) Estejam em condições de segurança e não sejam sujeitos a condições inapropriadas de calor, frio, luz, humidade ou outros factores adversos, nem à acção de microrganismos ou agentes infestantes._
_9.5 - Os medicamentos que necessitem de controlo da temperatura durante o armazenamento devem igualmente ser transportados em condições especiais adequadas.(...)"_.

EN: 
*_Can the pharmacy send medicines by post or courier?_*

_No. Legislation requires that medicines must be delivered to the home in compliance with the rules on supervision, qualification and adequate training for the dispensing of medicines, and in accordance with the transport rules set out in the Good Distribution Practices of Medicines._

The Good Distribution Practices of Medicines establish that:
_“(...) 9.4 – Medicines must be transported throughout their entire route in such a way that:_
_a) Their identification is not lost;_
_b) They do not contaminate nor are contaminated by other products or materials;_
_c) Special precautions are taken against spillage, breakage or theft;_
_d) They are kept in safe conditions and not subjected to inappropriate conditions of heat, cold, light, humidity or other adverse factors, nor to the action of microorganisms or pests._
_9.5 – Medicines requiring temperature control during storage must also be transported under appropriate special conditions. (...)”_

So, again, therefore, although this could be considered a grey area, INFARMED’s position appears to be clear, even if the response is supported by other considerations.

For this reason, we believe that, although the primary liability lies with the pharmacy, as they are the direct addressees of the applicable regulation, *Bolt can still be questioned* *by the authorities* *and might be subject to fines*, and +*we should remain mindful of this risk*+.

In case it is decided to move forward, besides the risks that were flagged:

# *Operational Considerations:*

* Bolt cannot guarantee that a courier will voluntarily return an undelivered order to the pharmacy. However, we can commit to directing the courier back to the pharmacy when delivery is not possible.
* Concerning the _not delivering simultaneously any other order from other partners_ we think there isn’t a major problem, as long as you are operationally able to do this. We just need to make it clear that we can only provide such assurance with respect to Bolt deliveries, but not regarding deliveries from other platforms that the courier may be carrying out.
* We should be prepared to compensate couriers in cases where they are required to return orders to the pharmacy.
* Customer Support (CS) teams must be fully briefed on this process so they can provide clear instructions to couriers who encounter delivery issues.
* As per article 3(2) of _Portaria n.º 1427/2007_ _,_ _“the dispensing of medicines with home delivery is limited to the municipality where the pharmacy is located and to the neighbouring municipalities”._

Hi [~accountid:712020:dc012e17-7e04-4ad8-8750-81fc7f7c6047] - I’ve added some comments to the document, which can be summarised as:

* It makes sense to me for Bolt / the industry to support measures that are generally objectionable e.g. child gambling, shaming users etc. This may help our other representations feel more reasonable.
* We are all suffering from regulation fatigue. This is in part because there are so many ‘principle based’ requirements. Rules are easier to follow and help ensure alignment.

I’ll keep the most sensitive points in this ticket as background to help guide and shape your representations:

* *High-level lines of argumentation for further thought / articulation:*  
** Any additional restrictions on pricing should not undermine our ability to respond to market dynamics. Platforms need flexibility to adjust in real time to supply and demand.
** We also act on behalf of service providers who rely on us to secure optimal pricing, drawing on our ability to observe and react to real-time market conditions.
** An individual’s prior history may indicate whether there is demand (or lack thereof) for lower pricing. Likewise, a history of ordering higher-end services may suggest that this is the appropriate level of service to present. Such approaches to personal pricing improve market efficiency and enhance our ability to match users with services at prices that work for them. This is not about “extorting” users, but about ensuring efficiency and alignment between demand and supply.

* *Our commercial narrative:* 
** We evaluate each ride separately. A key reason for unfulfilled rides is often the pricing point. Using different metrics and user-specific information, we aim to identify the appropriate price for each order. 
** At the same time, we are moving away from traditional incentives such as kick-back commissions or promo codes. 
** Where Bolt does earn more from a ride (for example, due to higher commission), those funds are reinvested into the market by lowering commission on subsequent orders. Our aim is not to extract more commission overall, but to stimulate greater activity on the platform, grow GMV, and increase market share.

* *We should guard against future dynamic commission and pricing practices where relevant, but be cautious with external messaging:*
** We may reduce our rate of commission in response to supply and demand (e.g. rates of 20% or lower). If riders demand lower pricing, we waive our right to charge the highest rate so that drivers are not impacted. This is commercially reasonable, as it allows us to adjust to user pools that require lower pricing.
** The sensitivity lies in how this could be framed externally: it risks being interpreted as “Bolt is the service provider, fully controlling pricing and deciding what drivers are paid.” In particular, if Bolt were to increase commission during a surge, that would present unfavourably.

State Secretary Approves Form 62 for Pillar Two Reporting

The Secretary of State for Tax Affairs has issued an ordinance approving the official registration Form 62 for the purpose of Pillar Two and respective filing instructions, as part of the Global Minimum Tax (GMT) regime, established by Law No. 41/2024, of 8 November 2024.

This form aims to ensure compliance with registration obligations for constituent entities located in Portugal that are part of corporate groups subject to the GMT regime. It also serves to notify the commencement of the application of this regime to large domestic enterprise groups, as well as to multinational enterprise (MNE) groups starting their international activity.

Furthermore, this form must be filed by each constituent entity in Portugal or, alternatively, by a designated local on behalf of all constituent entities (provided that the others confirm such nomination within 15 days via the Portuguese tax authorities' website). The form must be filed on or before the last day of the 9th month following the end of the relevant tax year (or up to last day of the 12th month following the end of the relevant tax year, for the first year under the GMT regime). For MNE groups whose tax year matches the calendar year, the first form (for 2024) is due by 31 December 2025.

The form remains valid in subsequent tax years if no changes occur (e.g. group composition) that require the filing of a new form.

In the case of late or missing filing, penalties between EUR 5,000 and EUR 100,000, plus 5% per day of delay, may apply. Further, in the case of errors or omissions, penalties between EUR 500 and EUR 23,500 may apply (without impacting the possibility of obtaining a relief from the same in the initial years under certain conditions).

The above update is issued by way of Ordinance No. 290/2025/1, of 2 September 2025, and is available [+here+|https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2025/09/16800/0000200007.pdf] (as a PDF and in Portuguese only).

FYI from UK: 

*HMRC Issues Guidance on Registration and Reporting of Pillar Two Top-Up Taxes*

The UK tax authority, His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC), has published guidance on the registration criteria and reporting deadlines under the United Kingdom's Pillar Two top-up taxes: the multinational top-up tax and the domestic top-up tax.

In the guidance on registration ([+here+|https://www.gov.uk/guidance/check-if-you-need-to-report-pillar-2-top-up-taxes]), HMRC reminds groups that taxpayers must register for Pillar Two top-up taxes if they have:

|at least one entity located in the UK; and|
|consolidated group annual revenues of EUR 750 million or more, in at least two of the previous four accounting periods.|

References to "groups" includes single entities.

The "filing member" of the eligible group must register even if they do not have to pay any top-up tax. Registration must take place within 6 months after the end of the first accounting period in which the above criteria are met.

If the group only has entities located in the United Kingdom, it must register to report for domestic top-up tax. If there are entities both in and outside the United Kingdom, registration must be for both domestic and multinational top-up taxes.

More information on registration can be found at [+Pillar 2 Top-up Taxes registration (notice 1)+|https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/pillar-2-top-up-taxes-registration-notice-1].

The filing member of a group must register online on the HMRC website [+here+|https://www.gov.uk/guidance/register-to-report-pillar-2-top-up-taxes], which also has details of the information that will be required during the registration process. The filing member will be either:

|the ultimate parent entity; or|
|another company group member nominated by the ultimate parent entity.|

The ultimate parent entity is the entity at the top of the group ownership structure. It is not a subsidiary of any other entity.

Once a group has registered to report Pillar Two top-up taxes, returns must be submitted on or before the deadline. The deadline for the initial report is 18 months after the end of the first accounting period, with subsequent reports being due 15 months after the end of the accounting period. Penalties may be applied if reports are late.

More information on penalties can be found in HMRC's [+Multinational Top-up Tax and Domestic Top-up Tax manual+|https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/multinational-top-up-tax-and-domestic-top-up-tax/mtt55400].

HMRC's guidance on how to report top-up taxes, which was published on 1 September 2025, can be found [+here+|https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-report-pillar-2-top-up-taxes].

Revenue Issues Guidance on Pillar Two Registration, Sets 31 December 2025 Deadline for In-Scope Entities

Revenue has issued new [+Tax and Duty Manual - Global Minimum Level of Taxation for Multinational Enterprise Groups and Large-Scale Domestic Groups in the Union – Administration+|https://www.revenue.ie/en/tax-professionals/tdm/income-tax-capital-gains-tax-corporation-tax/part-04a/04A-01-01A.pdf], confirming that in-scope entities under Pillar Two must register with Revenue by 31 December 2025.

The guidance confirms that entities within the scope of Pillar Two taxes (i.e. the Income Inclusion Rule (IIR), Undertaxed Profits Rule (UTPR), or Domestic Top-up Tax) must register for the relevant taxes with Revenue no later than 12 months after the last day of the first fiscal year in which they become subject to the relevant tax.

Thus, where an entity with a fiscal year ending on or before 31 December 2024 becomes liable to IIR top-up tax and domestic top-up tax in 2024, the entity must register for these taxes by 31 December 2025. Where an entity with a fiscal year ending on or before 31 December 2025 becomes liable to UTPR top-up tax in 2025, it must register for UTPR top-up tax by 31 December 2026. Registration is a one-time process and does not need to be repeated annually. Failure to comply with registration requirements may give rise to a penalty of EUR 10,000.

For previous reporting, _see_ [+Revenue Issues Guidance on Calculation of Deferred Tax Assets Under Pillar Two Rules (19 February 2025)+|https://research.ibfd.org/#/doc?url=/linkresolver/static/tns_2025-02-19_ie_1] and [+Revenue Clarifies Entity Jurisdiction, Administrative Matters Under Pillar Two Rules (19 December 2024)+|https://research.ibfd.org/#/doc?url=/linkresolver/static/tns_2024-12-19_ie_1].

SST a single-stage tax which is charge only once when: 1) Goods are manufactured in Malaysia by a registered manufacturer, or 2) 
Goods are imported into Malaysia (Customs collects it). After that stage, when the goods move through the supply chain (wholesaler → retailer → customer), no further Sales Tax is charged. Therefore, depending on who is the supplier, the SST should be charged for the goods or not. All the domestic purchase of goods invoices received during the last 2 years have not included SST. 


I believe that if we map them as “domestic purchase of goods” and the tax rate for such goods, when the invoice is 0% (which will be most of the cases), it will go to a human. Please see a general comment about the bailiff orders concerning independent drivers/couriers. *There is no need to create a legal ticket for every bailiff request - the requests shall be processed by the CS team following below without engaging legal.*  Please always communicate with the bailiff if something is unclear. Be proactive -  if you have questions, send emails/call bailiffs, it will help you to resolve the matter quicker. 

 There could be two types of bailiff orders:

# If the request relates to monthly payout *deductions*, we can explain to the bailiff the type of Bolt’s engagement with the drivers and see what he/she answers, explain to the bailiff the following issues:
#* Drivers/couriers are independent service providers (LHV, FIE, OU) and not Bolt’s employees. Thus, instead of a salary, 1) the drivers get a commission for their services rendered, whereas 2) couriers get the delivery fee for delivered orders.  Because of that, Bolt does not collect or analyze the data on how the amount of commissions/delivery fee paid correlates with the minimum subsistence level and what applicable taxes are for each driver;
#* Drivers/couriers are free to choose their working hours as well as the number of hours worked per week. Therefore, the remuneration earned by the drivers/couriers may vary greatly from week to week. In view of the stated, Bolt is not informed on how it should properly calculate and make deductions from so significantly fluctuating payouts;
Due to the above reasons, it is difficult for Bolt to comply with the bailiff’s request.
#* Drivers get commissions (delivery fee for couriers) via bank transfer to their business accounts. The commissions / delivery fees are never paid in cash. Thus, *the bailiffs themselves can deduct sums directly from the debtor’s bank account without Bolt’s engagements.*
# If the order stipulates that *funds are arrested* (seized or attached), *we shall comply with the request without any objections in that case:*
##  send a proper email notice to the bailiff acknowledging the receipt of the order and confirming that we will comply. Also, we ask the bailiff to update us on when we can change the bank account back to the driver's/courier’s bank account
## inform the driver/courier that his/her account is seized and as of XX date the payouts will be made in favour of the third party (*don't* disclose this third party) based on the bailiff's order No XXX (to manage the driver's/courier’s expectations, a driver/courier should also be informed in case only a certain amount is deducted from its payouts)
## chance the bank account per the request
## after a while once the bailiff's approval is received, change the bank account back and notify the driver/courier accordingly.

Hey,

In Slovakia we have commission netting.

_Through commission netting, your campaigns/bonuses/compensations are reflected as a discount from your commission, instead of each having their individual invoices. Simply, your commission is reduced in the amount of your campaigns/bonuses/compensations - ensuring a more clear invoicing process, and less invoicing noise._

_For example, previously you would see a commission of 416.91€ and separate bonus lines of 11€ on your invoice, which totaled up to 361.92€. Now, you would only see a single row of commission in the amount of 361.92€, meaning the calculation is already done in the background._

Nikolay Roll

For Italy: removing the _top-up_ option is a restrictive change for consumers, since they lose a feature they were already using. Even if our T&Cs don’t expressly regulate this, we cannot implement it silently.

* Arts. 20–23 of the Italian Consumer Code (D.lgs. 206/2005, implementing Directive 2005/29/EC) prohibit unfair commercial practices, including omissions or surprise changes that materially affect the consumer’s decision.
* The AGCM’s practice is that when a service limitation affects consumer rights or use of the product, companies must give adequate prior notice.

*Recommendation:* notify customers in advance. A *15-day notice period* is consistent with normal commercial practice. 

thanks

Hello! 

All of this information is already available in our internal processes for CS to guide drivers (like disabling cash payments). We create FAQ articles for legal requirements or for issues that causing significant volumes. Also, driver guides are meant to help with such information as well.

This is a very important topic for Customer Support. At the moment, we face significant issues when an SD ticket is created by an agent but other people cannot access it because it can’t be added via the link to the ticket directly. 

In practice, in our daily work tickets often need to be escalated to the in-house team, taken over by other outsourcing suppliers, or reopened by different agents. This means that the agent who initially created the ticket *cannot* proactively add all relevant people to ensure full visibility = there is no way to make sure that we can avoid situations when ticket is not visible to other agents. This could be fixed only if the “add via link” feature will be added to all SD types.

The problem becomes especially critical when the ticket creator goes on vacation or leaves the company. In such cases, the ticket is essentially lost, and regaining access requires multiple unnecessary steps.

Allowing *all SD ticket types* to be added via link (without requiring full integration!) would bring a major improvement. Currently, agents can spend up to 20 minutes simply trying to:

* identify the ticket creator,
* reach out to them,
* request access,
* wait for a reply and wait until the creator adds them to the SD.

This process is inefficient, messy, and not user-friendly, especially since the "add link" feature already exists. When the feature was first announced, we understood it to apply to all SD tickets, not just the few that are fully integrated. Otherwise, the value is very limited: if a ticket type is fully integrated, it can already be created directly in Beehive, so linking is redundant. The real purpose of linking should be for SDs *without full integration*, so that visibility can be maintained.

Currently, many high-volume SDs (for example, all tech support tickets) are not supported as full integration, so making adding a feature “via link” would just improve CS work at 100%. Really, I am not overreacting 🙂 This is one of the most common concerns I hear about almost every day.

We would highly appreciate it if your team could prioritize this improvement, as it would have a direct impact on our efficiency and average handling time. Thank you!

_To give you further comfort, we are ready to clarify in the agreement that users benefit from insurance taken out by the independent service providers as required by law, and, where applicable, from additional coverage arranged by Bolt. # Clause 3.2 - what they’ve requested we can’t do. You may use as an explanation something like this:
_Clause 3.2 reflects the fact that the Customer controls who is added or removed from the business account and therefore must cover any exceptional costs arising from those users’ actions (e.g. fines, misuse). This obligation cannot be mutual, because Bolt does not control the Customer’s tax position, nor can Bolt indemnify against how local tax law applies to your business. Bolt fully complies with its own tax obligations and provides proper invoices; the Customer’s corporate tax treatment is independent of Bolt and cannot be transferred as a contractual risk._
# The exclusions in Clause 6.3(IV) are standard for SaaS and marketplace agreements and are designed to prevent speculative or disproportionate claims far exceeding the value of the contract. To clarify:
– “Pure economic loss” means purely financial damages without direct connection to physical damage or personal injury (e.g. reputational harm, lost investment opportunity).
– “Indirect or consequential losses” refer to losses that are not the immediate result of an issue, but arise as a secondary effect (e.g. lost profit from a missed business opportunity).
– “Special damages” are losses that are unusual or unique to the Customer’s particular circumstances, which Bolt could not reasonably foresee.

Additional comments on [Move EU draft lobbying responses|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mBiuqf3Etk8V3UQlJkY917NEQ4qeWEA_/edit]:

[~accountid:712020:dc012e17-7e04-4ad8-8750-81fc7f7c6047] - I’ve looked at the Move EU document and my comments from the EUTA doc largely carry over. Restating them:

* It makes sense for Bolt and the industry to back clearly objectionable measures (e.g. child gambling, user shaming), as this makes our other positions seem more reasonable.
* Regulation fatigue is growing, driven by vague ‘principle-based’ requirements. Clear rules are easier to follow and ensure alignment.
* See also my other comments in respect of lines of argumentation that you could add. 

As for the comments on behalf of Uber, the following came to mind (please take what you like and leave what you don’t):

* There are multiple references to platforms ‘ensuring fairness’ and ‘avoiding imbalance’. Personally, I dislike this framing. Bolt should not present itself as the ‘arbiter of fairness’. Our role is to react in real time to market conditions, and dynamic pricing is one of the key ways we do so. For example, prices may be adjusted downwards if customers are demanding lower pricing. The narrative should be that the market drives outcomes, not Bolt / platforms.
* Dynamic pricing should also not be confused with personal pricing. General pricing may be adjusted to reflect the purchasing power of the customer base, but all customers are then shown the same price. This is very different from presenting two customers with different prices for the same service — which is what the regulation is likely targeting. The goal should therefore be to ensure that new rules do not curb legitimate, non-discriminatory dynamic pricing practices. 
* Just so you are aware, Bolt is intending to explore personal pricing as described above (different prices for different customers).
* There was a reference to the EU focusing only on consumers, not drivers. Depending on how legislation is framed, however, drivers and fleets could also be considered ‘consumers/users’ of the platform. For that reason, we should aim to explain how the platform works in general, not only from the perspective of riders.
* Finally, I did not see Uber reference commission. Dynamic commission practices are particularly sensitive, so we should be cautious about discussing them externally, even if we expect Uber also uses them.

Let me know if you have any questions 🙏

*Quick update – Updated Cognito Breach Assessment (first draft finalised)*

* *Draft available in the spreadsheet under “WIP – Updated Breach Risk Assessment”* tab [HERE|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M1z30znr9t80F_kQMtNNRzsA-8BUp3LZTMasmAHBNsE/edit?gid=690450369#gid=690450369].
** My edits are marked in *red*.
** Both *questions* and *calculation methodology* have been updated.

* *Main approach I followed when updating the assessment:*
** Added missing fields based on feedback from Project Panther such as _"Bolt entity reporting", "Link to notification:_" etc.
** Reviewed and integrated feedback from counsels.
** Aligned with ICO and CNIL breach forms, adding relevant suggestions.
** Reviewed previous Cognito assessments and added:
*** Types of data
*** Bolt-specific factors to decrease breach risk (e.g., recycled phone numbers).
** Summarised data types using privacy notices, past breaches, and ENISA methodology.
** I’ve removed the final wording on whether a breach _is reportable to DPA/data subjects._ Going forward, the assessment will focus on the *severity score (SE)* and *breach details (e.g. country, scope of data).*
*** Logic behind: Given that in some countries the reporting threshold is higher (e.g., EEA, UK) and in others lower (e.g., South Africa, Ghana), I aimed to make the breach assessment more universal in case it needs to be shared externally.

* *Structure: the updated assessment consists of 9 sections (8 scored):*
*# General information
*# Number of affected data subjects
*# Type of affected data subjects
*# Type of affected personal data
*# Possible adverse effects on individuals
*# Contextual factors decreasing risks
*# Ease of identification of the data subject
*# Circumstances + intent
*# Contextual factors decreasing risks (consolidated scoring)

* *Scoring formula for the Severity Score (SE):*
** *SE = [Number of Data Subjects] + [Type of Data Subjects] + [Type of Personal Data] + [Possible Adverse Effects] + [Ease of Identification] + [Circumstances (CIA + intent)] – [Contextual Factors Decreasing Risks]*
*** I’ve added explanations in *column O (“Comments”)* to clarify how calculations are done.
**** It is important as in some section we need to the take the highest baseline score, whereas in others we add all the applicable scores. I will explain this during the team call on Oct 13th.

* *Next steps:*
** Since next week we’ll be onsite, I plan to share this draft with Privacy Legal the week after (w/c October 13th) to gather feedback before asking Greg to update it in Cognito and upload it into Relaynce.
** I’ll also present the main edits (questions + methodology) in the *Team Call on Monday, October 13th*

Hello team, 
[~accountid:712020:f0e74860-330c-44ed-9e8f-e89de3fd8d5c], I understood that the agreements for the cities was already suitable, since the parties wanted to sign it, so it’s a bit strange that they are still coming back with changes.

As I understand it, negotiating with municipalities rarely succeeds, and in most cases Bolt, if it wants to operate within a municipality’s territory, has little choice but to accept the conditions imposed by the municipality.

*That said, we can still try to negotiate. Here are my thoughts:*


*1. Clause 1.6 – Cost Recovery*

* I believe that under Swiss law, even if the contractual clause is removed, Bolt still has a statutory right to claim damages for breach of contract. However, recovery is not automatic — Bolt must prove causation and quantify damages, which is slower and riskier.

Our options here is to propose more friendly clauses to the municipality:
*Option A – Narrowed, Reasonable Costs*

_“If the Municipality, without justified reason, delays or fails to perform its obligations under this Agreement, Bolt may recover from the Municipality the_ *_reasonable, documented and direct costs_* _necessarily incurred as a result of such delay or failure, provided that such costs are proportionate and directly linked to the Municipality’s default.”_

*Option B – Capped Recovery (for predictability)*

_“If the Municipality, without justified reason, delays or fails to perform its obligations under this Agreement, Bolt may recover from the Municipality the_ *_reasonable, documented direct costs_* _necessarily incurred as a result, up to a maximum of [CHF X] per month or [Y% of the applicable monthly service fee].”_



*2. Clause 7.3 – Allocation of Costs*

In this situation, if the clause is kept, Bolt is protected, because anything not specified in the agreement is not Bolt’s headache - it becomes the municipality’s problem. However, if this clause is removed, the situation flips completely. Therefore, I would suggest a compromise solution in this case:
_“Each party bears its own costs unless otherwise expressly agreed. Costs specific to the municipality’s public infrastructure remain the municipality’s responsibility.”._

# *Clause 11.1 – Liability for Infrastructure*

I believe that the clause is essentially restating statutory law, so deletion of this clause should not increase Bolt’s liability directly, because the law is mandatory. However, I think that we can suggest this amendment instead: 

“For the avoidance of doubt, the Municipality remains responsible for the safety and maintenance of public infrastructure under applicable law.”.

Let me know if you have any additional questions, thanks!

Hi [~accountid:60cdaa478f2cc1006978c4a0] 👋 

We cannot share the reporter’s video or detailed safety report with the Fleet Owner. Both contain personal data and sensitive information that would violate GDPR and Bolt’s confidentiality commitments. The only compliant path is to respond to the FO in a way that informs them that a driver suspension/termination occurred due to serious safety concerns, without disclosing evidence or complainant details.

*_What we can share_*

* A *generic explanation* that the driver’s account was blocked due to a serious safety-related concern (sexual misconduct/inappropriate conduct), framed as a breach of Bolt’s platform rules.
* The *current account action* (temporary suspension vs permanent block).
* The *next steps available to the Fleet Owner* (e.g., they may speak to their driver, gather internal documentation, and share feedback with Bolt).
* Reassurance that the decision is finalised by Bolt’s Safety Team following internal review.

*_Recommended response to the FO_*

* Politely reject the request for access to video or the full safety report.
* Reinforce that Bolt takes such allegations seriously and acts in line with its duty of care to passengers and drivers.



I suggest using this response (this is a template proposed by Central Ops Safety - but you can adjust as appropriate):

{quote}_Dear [Fleet Owner Name],_

_We would like to inform you that the account of driver_ *_[Driver Full Name / Driver ID]_*_, associated with your fleet, has been_ *_[temporarily suspended / permanently blocked]_* _on our platform due to a_ *_serious safety-related concern which constitutes a breach of our terms related to  [INSERT general description of the driver’s behavior: inappropriate comments, unsolicited physical contact attempts, or actions that made passengers feel unsafe]_*_._

_While we are unable to share the specific details of the case due to privacy regulations, please find below relevant information and next steps if you wish to connect with The Bolt Safety Team:_

I analyzed the situation of repeated cases with ChatGPT deep research based on data from [here|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/rental/etl_fact_micromobility_tasks_resolved?toggle=fil&qid=Ii2pAW9TY3w3FuMTxHKsqy]. Here are the most important conclusions:

* Majority of vehicles (77%) have 4 or less collections within 12 months:

!image-20251003-133117.png|width=1218,height=780,alt="image-20251003-133117.png"!

h2. City-based analysis:

!image-20251003-133547.png|width=1215,height=780,alt="image-20251003-133547.png"!

* *Oslo* stands out as having the most severe repeat-collection problem. Oslo’s vehicles had a median of 4 collections each (compared to 2–3 in other large cities), and nearly *45% of Oslo’s vehicles had 5 or more collections over the year*. In fact, *6.3% of Oslo vehicles had at least 10 collections*. This indicates a high incidence of vehicles requiring frequent intervention. The worst-offending vehicle in Oslo had 42 collections, suggesting chronic issues (e.g. persistent vandalism or mechanical problems requiring repeated pickup).
* *Brussels* also shows high offender rates. *38% of Brussels vehicles had ≥5 collections*【46†】, and about 4.2% had ≥10. The median per-vehicle in Brussels was 4 collections, with a maximum of 36. Brussels and Oslo clearly form a cluster of cities with *much heavier collection activity per vehicle* and many repeat offenders.
* *Munich* had moderate repeat issues: median ~3 collections per vehicle. About *16.6% of Munich’s fleet had 5+ collections* (and ~1.1% had ≥10). The worst Munich vehicle had 16 collections. Munich’s distribution indicates *some* outliers but far fewer than Oslo/Brussels; most Munich vehicles required only occasional collections.
* *Frankfurt* and *Düsseldorf* show similar patterns to each other: median ~3, and about *10% of vehicles with ≥5 collections* (very few above 10: only ~0.3–0.4%). These cities have moderate overall collection rates but comparatively _fewer_ extreme outliers. The maximums were 17 (Frankfurt) and 25 (Düsseldorf) collections on a single vehicle – high, but such cases were isolated.
* *Stuttgart* had the mildest pattern among the major cities. The median was just 2 collections per vehicle, and only *~3.3% of vehicles had 5 or more*【46†】. Virtually no Stuttgart vehicle exceeded 10 collections (max was 13). This suggests Stuttgart’s fleet had relatively stable operations with few repeat-problem vehicles.

h2. Monthly Trends in Repeat Offenders

Using the chosen threshold (≥3 collections in 14 days), we identified *when* repeat offenses occurred and how their frequency evolved over time in each city. *Figure 3* shows the month-by-month percentage of active vehicles that were repeat offenders in each city

!image-20251003-133906.png|width=1579,height=1180,alt="image-20251003-133906.png"!

* *Oslo’s repeat-offender rate spiked dramatically in early 2025.* Through late 2024, Oslo had a low baseline (~2–3% of vehicles flagged). But in *Feb–Mar 2025, it jumped to ~9–11%* of active vehicles. This corresponds to a surge of vehicles hitting 3 collections in 2 weeks during the winter when we had huge problems with *drum brakes corrosion*. After March, Oslo’s rate declined, falling to ~6% by summer and ending around ~5% in Sep 2025.
* *Brussels saw a steady rise in repeat offenders over the year.* Starting around 1–2% in late 2024, Brussels climbed to ~5–6% by summer 2025, peaking at *~6.5% in August–September 2025*. Unlike Oslo’s spike, Brussels’ increase was more gradual, indicating a growing underlying issue. By late 2025, Brussels nearly matched Oslo in repeat-offender share. This upward trend may reflect accumulating wear-and-tear on the fleet or other factors gradually increasing collection frequency.
* *Munich* had a relatively *flat, low* repeat-offender rate, mostly *1–2%* throughout, ticking up slightly to ~2.5% in Aug 2025. There was no dramatic surge – Munich appears stable, with only a small fraction of vehicles repeatedly collected in any month.
* *Frankfurt and Düsseldorf* also stayed low. Both hovered around *1% or less for most of the year*, with minor bumps to ~1.5–2% in some summer months. 
* *Stuttgart* was near zero for long stretches – many months saw _no_ repeat offenders at all – with only tiny upticks (e.g. ~1–2% in a couple of months toward the end). These cities maintained consistently low repeat-problem rates over time.

Hey, [~accountid:5d95f00136d2520dde7ede17],

*a) Options*
*From riskiest to safest in your proposed scenarios:*

# *Direct top-ups to driver balance*: clearest employment/tax risk, can look like income. 
# *Bolt pays 100% to school for named drivers*: still high risk, as it can be seen as individualised benefit.
# *Partial coverage (e.g. 90/10 split)* and *group-based arrangements or voucher systems*: lower risk, looks more like _support program,_ rather than employment perk.

Maybe instead of Bolt paying, *negotiate discounted rates with language schools* and let drivers pay directly. That way Bolt facilitates access but avoids financial entanglement.



*What Bolt could also consider:*

* *Prefer vouchers / group purchase*: Bolt buys X amount of course seats or generic vouchers from schools, then distributes them. This can look less like Bolt directly paying driver’s personal expense and more like a neutral support program.
* *Contracts with schools*: Frame Bolt’s role as _bulk purchaser_ or _sponsor_, not “employer paying for staff training.”
* *Driver communications*: Emphasise voluntariness, neutrality, and that this is a _public interest initiative_ to support integration, not a requirement of being on the platform.
* *Group vs. individual*: Group is safer (less individualised, easier to defend as general support). 
* *Co-payment (even symbolic)*: Having drivers contribute even 10% helps underline independence and reduces reclass risk.

*b) Term*

All laws are part of a single legal system, so to avoid contradictions, the legislator tends to use already defined concepts, unless *it specifically wishes to establish a new or different meaning*.
Law (LR įstatymas dėl užsieniečių teisinės padėties) 1 art. 1 p. states, “Šis *Įstatymas nustato užsieniečių* atvykimo ir išvykimo, *buvimo ir gyvenimo*, prieglobsčio ir laikinosios apsaugos Lietuvos Respublikoje suteikimo, *integracijos* ir sprendimų dėl užsieniečių teisinės padėties apskundimo tvarką *ir kitus užsieniečių teisinės padėties Lietuvos Respublikoje klausimus*, taip pat reglamentuoja Lietuvos Respublikos elektroninio rezidento statuso suteikimo ir panaikinimo sąlygas ir tvarką.”, so this law and it’s definitions covers our situation and language law.

If in the language law certain terms should be understood differently than they are defined in the Law of the Legal Status of Aliens (LR įstatymas dėl užsieniečių teisinės padėties), such terms would be provided in Article 2 of the language law.

According to German regulation (§ 67 paragraph 8 StVZO), the front reflector installation height is between 400 and 1200mm.

However according to UNECE R48 (*Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to the installation of lighting and light-signalling devices*) the front reflector installation height is not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm, but it also says that up to 1500mm is allowed, if the vehicle design demands it.

{quote}_6.16.4.2.   In height: above the ground, not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (1 500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm)._{quote}



So in conclusion; if we are below 1200mm with the center of the front reflector, we are good to go in Germany and also fall within the exception range of UNECE R48.

If you need a *report*, please refer to FleetX (DriverX). If your request concerns an *invoice*, follow these steps:

   * If you encounter any other error, please let us know.
5. Commission invoices for the entire history of the fleet/driver are available either under **Invoice tasks** or **Partner Invoices**.

Maintenance is only enforced during {{VALIDATE_TOPOLOGY_V2}}. If maintenance is enabled after validation (while a pipeline is pending approvals), the pipeline proceeds on approval because neither {{WAIT_FOR_PIPELINE_APPROVALS}} nor {{REQUEST_LOCK}} re-checks cluster maintenance.

h3. Minimal-risk fix

Add a maintenance guard as close to execution as possible. Two complementary options:

* Option A (recommended): Re-check maintenance at approval time.

* Inject {{ClusterMaintenanceService}} into {{WaitForPipelineApprovalsStateProcessor}}.

* Before returning the transition to {{REQUEST_LOCK}}, fetch maintenance state and throw if any {{payload.locations[*].cluster_name}} is under maintenance.

* Option B (defense in depth): Block at lock time.

* Inject {{ClusterMaintenanceService}} into {{RequestLockStateProcessor}}.

* Before calling {{requestLock}}, check each lock’s {{cluster}} against maintenance and throw if under maintenance.

For CREATE statement flows that may not use locks, add the same check in {{InitiateDispatchStateProcessor}} before branching, to ensure consistent behavior.

Key Issues for Review – rescue .co (RC) Membership Agreement

There are several points that warrant internal alignment and further discussion - [~accountid:5f64ab01cc17bd006f2a0a58]  your input would also be much appreciated here as these areas may simply require clarification on the intended roll out of this venture-

* *Liability Cap – Clause 11.4:*
The supplier’s liability is capped at the value of the membership fees only, with no exceptions for serious issues such as gross negligence, data breach, or service failure. This may expose Bolt to reputational or operational risks, particularly where third-party beneficiaries (riders/drivers) are involved.
* *Lack of Supplier Indemnity – Clause 11.1 (also see Clause 11.3):*
There is no indemnity in favour of Bolt in respect of claims by third parties (e.g. riders, drivers, or regulators) arising from RC’s failure, negligence, or data breach. While Clause 11.1 imposes indemnity obligations on “Members”, these are defined as the riders/drivers — not Bolt. Since they are not contracting parties, enforcement and allocation of liability remain unclear.
* *No SLAs / Performance Standards – Clauses 4.1.1 to 4.1.7 (Service Description):*
The agreement does not contain any service level commitments (e.g. response times) or minimum performance standards. This weakens enforceability in the event of poor performance or delayed response in emergency situations.
* *Termination for Convenience – Clause 10.2:*
While termination for convenience appears to be allowed with 30 days’ notice, the language regarding "fully paid-up obligations" is vague. It is unclear whether Bolt would remain liable for the entire contract value even if it terminates early.
* *Unilateral Changes to Terms – Clause 10.4 / 11.10:*
RC may unilaterally amend the terms of the agreement with only 30 or 7 days’ notice, depending on the clause relied on. This limits contractual stability and could allow material changes without Bolt's agreement.
* *Automatic Renewal – Clause 2.4 / 10.1:*
The agreement auto-renews for a further two years unless cancelled 60 days prior to expiry. 
* *Exclusion of Refunds – Clause 10.3:*
Fees are stated to be non-refundable upon termination, including where service has not been fully utilised. This could result in stranded costs for Bolt if early termination is necessary.
* *Discretionary Service Denial – Clause 4.1.6 / 5.3 / 8.1.3:*
RC has broad discretion to decline service requests based on its internal assessment of what constitutes an “emergency”. This may lead to inconsistent application or denial of critical services without recourse.
* *Third-Party Provider Disclaimer – Clause 11.3:*
RC disclaims responsibility for the performance or conduct of the emergency service providers it dispatches (ambulance, security, etc.). This creates a gap in accountability if service delivery fails.

Flagging a few potential areas of concern around data in this arrangement:

The agreement involves collecting sensitive personal data (like health and location info) for drivers and riders, who aren’t actually parties to the contract. There aren’t any data breach notification obligations included, and data breaches also aren’t mentioned in the liability or indemnity provisions.

*Data Protection – Clause 11.16:*
There’s a general privacy clause, but no detailed data protection obligations.

*Data Access by Bolt – Clause 11.16:*
It looks like Bolt’s access to medical or incident-related data is quite limited. Might be worth checking whether we’d have the access needed for operations/audit etc.

The difference in two “debt reconciliation systems”: 


Most markets:  courier earnings are reconciled with the cash couriers have, e.g. the courier's earning from an order is €3. If courier gets €10 from eater, then the €3 is deducted from the cash at hand and the overall debt for the courier is €7 after delivering the order. And after that, let's say the courier delivers a non-cash order for which their earning is €2. After delivering that order, the courier's debt will become €5.


(ii) Estonia is different - the cash debt and courier earnings are not netted due to tax considerations. So using the same example, a courier in Estonia completes an order where they earn €3 and collect €10 in cash from the eater. Instead of netting these out, Bolt records the courier’s earnings balance as €3 and their cash debt balance as €10. When the courier later delivers a non-cash order worth €2, their earnings balance increases to €5, while the debt balance remains €10.
The courier still owes Bolt €10 separately for the cash, but the €5 are not netted, but are paid out to the courier separately.  Nothing is reconciled between the two balances. 

Because of tax regulations in Estonia, we transfer courier earnings only to the LHV Entrepreneur account, which deducts the taxes and pays the after-tax earnings to the couriers.  If we were to reconcile cash debt with earnings, then an amount that is lesser than the actual earnings (earnings minus cash debt) will get transferred to the LHV Entrepreneur account, which provides a loophole for couriers to pay tax on lesser than actual earnings. In the above example, the courier earnings are €3 and debt is €10. If the courier makes a couple of non-cash deliveries with total earnings of €7, then their earnings will equal debt. If we were to reconcile the debt with earnings, their balance would be 0 and nothing would be transferred to the LHV Entrepreneur account, which means the courier can get away with paying no tax even though income/earnings are €10.

As a result, we decided to split the balance into debt and earnings balances.

Following a request from Osi (Nigeria GM), and Konrad, we engaged Local Counsel (Pavestones) in Nigeria to give a formal legal opinion on our Biometric Database and to validate our existing research and understanding that there is no legal basis to proceed with the Biometric Database in Nigeria.

Pavestones confirmed this. However, we have brainstormed a potential compliance solution as follows:

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Scenario:*

* Embeddings are stored in a segregated environment with the following controls.
* Separate datastore with no driver IDs or metadata; no mapping table.
* Strict least-privilege and separation of duties so no individual/team has concurrent access to both embeddings and driver photos.
{panel}

The idea is to move away from processing ‘personal data’ or at least implement sufficient technical and organisational measures to make re-identification less likely/operationally impossible for Ops/CS.

We have followed up with Pavestones for their updated advice and are waiting to hear back.

Hi [~accountid:712020:7f456fc3-1ae4-4f6a-923a-a0a2d2ef5030] we have received the following update from outside counsel: 

_Further to our email below, please be informed that we were at the offices of the State Police Command, Ikeja, Lagos State today to honour the invitation extended to Bolt in respect of the above-captioned matter._

_At the State Command, we met with the Investigative Police Officer (IPO) detailed to the investigation of the matter, Inspector Owoleye Grace and her colleagues. In brief, the IPO informed us that the matter being investigated is a case of theft concerning one Tony Okakwu, a driver registered on the Bolt platform. The driver was reported to have stolen goods belonging to the complainant, therefore, the Police required the presence of the driver to get to the bottom of the matter._ 

_The IPO stated that the reason why Bolt was invited was to secure the presence of the driver, since the driver is registered on the Bolt platform. We explained to the police that drivers operating on the Bolt platform are not employees of Bolt, rather, they are independent contractors who access the platform whenever they wish to offer their services to members of the public._ 

_We further explained that the non-existence of an employment relationship between the driver and Bolt meant that Bolt is not responsible for any criminal actions committed by the driver. We stated that, nonetheless, Bolt always takes a strong stance against criminal activities, as it reports any drivers who have committed criminal actions to the Police and supports the Police whenever necessary._ 

_Having educated the IPO and her investigation team on the operations model of Bolt, the Team Lead in charge of the investigation agreed with us that Bolt could not be compelled to produce the driver. We stated that, nonetheless, Bolt would be willing to support the investigation by furnishing the Police with any relevant information in its custody which may be required to aid the investigation._  

_Following our interaction with the Police, the Team Lead resolved that Bolt's presence would no longer be required in the investigation, but he stated that the Police could reach out in respect of any assistance required to further the investigation._

_In the meantime, we shall continue to keep you updated as developments arise._



Accordingly, I will be closing the ticket. Please re-open if further legal assistance is required on this matter.
